Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Two
Hundred Nineteenth Report on Demands for Grants (2015-16) of the Ministry of Culture.

points raised by the Members.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 16th April, 2015.

REPORT
The Ministry of Culture is responsible for the preservation and conservation of the country's
rich cultural heritage and promotion of art and culture. The Ministry functions through two attached
offices, six subordinate offices and thirty five autonomous organisations. There are seven Zonal
Cultural Centres for promoting folk and traditional arts of different regions of the country. There are
also four National Missions viz., National Mission for Manuscripts, National Mission for Monuments
and Antiquities, National Mission on Libraries and Gandhi Heritage Sites Mission.
2. The vision of the Ministry has been to protect the cultural diversity of the country and its
heritage. The mission of the Ministry is to implement sustainable solution through which India's
diverse tangible and intangible culture and ancient heritage will remain universally acceptable.
3. The mandate of the Ministry is to preserve, promote & disseminate all forms of Art & Culture
through (i) Maintenance & Conservation of Heritage, Historical Sites & Ancient Monuments; (ii)
Promotion of Literary, Visual and Performing Arts through various organizations; (iii) Promotion of
Institutional & Individual Non-official Initiatives in Art & Culture; (iv) Administration of Museums to
ensure Preservation, Conservation and to facilitate Public Access to Heritage; (v) Administration of
Public Libraries; (vi) Maintenance of Manuscript Records and their digitization; (vii) Promotion of
Institutions & Organisations of Buddhist & Tibetan Studies; (viii) Preservation of Gandhian Heritage
Promotion of Research and Awareness in field of Art & Culture; (ix) Promotion of Research in
Anthropology & Ethnology; (x) Ensuring Equitable Access to Cultural Goods & Services for benefit
of all Members of the Community; (xi) Promotion of Cultural Industries including Traditional Artisanal
Enterprises; (xii) Catalysing Partnerships at every level to ensure Sustainable Development &
Management of Cultural Resources; (xiii) Promotion of International Cultural Relations; and (xiv)
Observation of Centenaries and Anniversaries of Important National Personalities & Events.
4. The Ministry is the custodian of all the major libraries in the country. It extends grant-in-aid
for library development and is also responsible for all policy matters regarding library development.
Through National Archives of India, the Ministry is responsible for maintenance of all archival records
of the country. The Ministry is involved in protection and promotion of Buddhist and Tibetan Culture
through various institutions located at Sarnath, Varanasi and Leh.
5. The Ministry has a capacity-building programme for all those who wish to excel in the field
of art and culture. Institutions like the School of Archaeology, School of Archives, National Museum
Institute, the Asiatic Society, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies are mentionable in
this regard. Various courses offered by National School of Drama and Kalakshetra Foundation are also
some of the examples of capacity building programmes of the Ministry.
6. The Ministry marks its international presence by way of organising Festivals of India abroad
and is also responsible for implementation of various UNESCO Conventions in the field of culture and
for inscribing world heritage sites.
7. The Budget allocations of the Ministry of Culture for the financial year 2015-16, contained
in Demand No. 20 was taken up for consideration by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture in its meeting held on the 31st March, 2015. The
Secretary and other officials of the Ministry of Culture and its subordinate Organisations made a

11. As against total budgetary provision of Rs. 2511.00 crore at BE 2014-15 which was reduced
to Rs. 2159.00 crore at RE 2014-15, the budget for 2015-16 for Ministry of Culture has been pegged
at Rs. 2169.00 crore, for undertaking various programmes/activities/projects under Plan & Non-Plan
Heads.
12. The Secretary, Ministry of Culture while making a presentation before the Committee, stated
that economy circulars have been put in place by the Government and that the Ministry has rigidly
adhered to the economy circulars in place by a reduction of 10% in Non-plan expenditure, reduction
in travel, seminars, conferences and workshops.
13. The Committee notes that the present Budget Estimates shows an increase of just
Rs.10 crores in comparison to the Revised Estimate last year  i.e.,  2014-15. The Committee is
also surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a sharp budgetary cut at RE stage in the
last financial year. The Committee failed to get a convincing reason for this cut. Given the
importance of the mandate of this Ministry  i.e,  to preserve, protect and promote our vast
cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible, spread across the length and breadth of the
country, the Committee is at a loss to see that Plan allocation to this Ministry has come down

3
from Rs.1835 crore in BE 2014-15 to Rs.1500 crore in RE 2014-15 and to Rs.1455 crore in BE
of 2015-16. Such allocation are highly insufficient and the Committee recommends that Plan
allocation for the Department be increased adequately at RE stage.

Spending pattern during the Twelfth Plan
17. As per the data furnished by the Ministry, during the first year of the 12th Five Year Plan, as
against Rs. 864.00 crore approved by the Planning Commission, the Ministry had incurred an
expenditure of Rs. 803.79 crore during the year 2012-13, which is about 93.03% of RE 2012-13.
18. During the year 2013-14, (the 2nd year of the 12th Five Year Plan - 2012-17, a sum of
Rs. 1537.00 crore was allocated for various developmental activities/programmes of the Ministry of
Culture, as against the outlay of Rs. 864.00 crore for the Annual Plan 2012-13. This plan allocation
included Rs. 102.00 crore (Rs. 100.00 crore for INTACH as corpus fund and Rs. 2.00 crore for
Kedarnath Temple) obtained in the 1st Batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants- 2013-14. The
Plan allocation showed an increase of 77.89% in for the Annual Plan 2013-14 over the year 2012-
13. The Annual Plan allocation was reduced to Rs. 1470.00 crore at the Revised Estimates stage
against which an expenditure of Rs. 1380.13 crore (93.89%) was incurred.
19. During the year 2014-15, an amount of Rs. 1835.00 crore was allocated to the Ministry for
the Annual Plan 2014-15, as against Rs. 1537.00 crore allocated for the year 2013-14. The increase
in plan allocation in 2014-15 was about 19.39% over the year 2013-14, against which expenditure
of Rs. 1285.84 crore (85.72%) as on 09/03/2015 has been incurred.
20. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry was able to spend more than 90%
of its allocation during the first three years of the Twelfth Plan. At the same time, the
Committee observes that better planning and supervision could have definitely improved the
pace of utilization.
2015-16
21. The Committee has been informed that for the Annual Plan 2015-16, Ministry of Finance has
allocated an amount of Rs. 1455.00 crore for 'Rashtriya Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana' under Ministry
of Culture, as against Rs. 2217.56 crore projected for 2015-16. This allocation has been earmarked
by the Ministry of Finance for re-structured six new heads/sectors viz. (i) Zonal Cultural Centers,
(ii) Scheme of Art & Culture and Centenary Celebrations, (iii) Archaeological Survey of India, (iv)
Museums, (v) Libraries and (vi) Archives Library and the existing sectors viz.,  Secretariat,
International Cultural Relations and Centenaries, Celebrations and Memorials, etc. have been
subsumed under the Scheme of Art & Culture and Centenary Celebrations from the year 2015-16.
22. The total Plan allocation of Rs. 1455.00 crore includes Rs. 77.50 crore for the Building
Projects of Attached & Subordinate offices under the Ministry, Rs. 29.10 crore earmarked for Tribal
Sub-Plan and Rs. 145.50 crore earmarked for promoting the unique cultural heritage of North Eastern
Region.

24. The Ministry stated that during 2015-16, an allocation of Rs.350.00 crore has been made for
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) by Ministry of Finance. Out of Rs.350.00 crore allocated to
ASI, an amount of Rs.20.00 crore has been allocated by the Ministry of Culture for undertaking
various Building Projects of ASI. This leaves a balance of Rs.330.00 crore for its activities including
Rs.5.00 crore for undertaking activities in North East Areas. The Ministry of Culture has requested
the Ministry of Finance to consider additional funds of Rs.60.00 crore to ASI for setting up of 25
Aadarsh Smarak (Model Monuments).
25. International Cultural Relations Scheme, Centenary Celebrations & Memorials and Secretariat
of MoC have been subsumed under the major group "Scheme of Art & Culture and Centenary
Celebrations", for which Plan allocation of Rs.500.00 crore has been made for the year 2015-16.
26. According to the Ministry, the such a group wise allocation into group-wise will enable the
Ministry to readjust or to re-appropriate funds to the needy scheme/organization from the individual
schemes/ organizations at appropriate time, subsumed within the group. The Ministry has stated that
the Plan allocations under each group with individual schemes/organizations have been worked out
and earmarked for each constituent (organization or scheme), keeping in view the requirements of
Plan funds for the activities of each organization / scheme, within the overall (Plan) allocation under
respective integrated heads. This exercise was carried out by the Ministry of Culture, in consultation
with all concerned officers and finalised with the approval of AS&FA (Culture) and Secretary
(Culture). These funds will be placed at the disposal of the respective Bureau Heads for deciding
release of Plan funds in favour of each scheme/institution during 2015-16.

7
27. The Committee notes that the group- wise allocation will help the Ministry to reallocate
funds among the Schemes subsumed within the group, when the need arises. The Committee
hopes that this financial arrangement would impart more flexibility to the Ministry in terms
of allocation, leading to optimum utilization of funds. Nevertheless, the Committee desires
that due care and caution should be exercised to ensure that the new scheme of allocation
does not affect the progress of existing schemes/ programmes of the Ministry and also the
functioning of vital Organisations under the Ministry. The Committee would like to emphasize
that the interse fund allocation of the grouped heads should be brought to the notice of the
Committee at appropriate time.
Ministry's Projected Demand vis-a-vis Budgetary allocation
28. The Ministry of Culture has stated that the Ministry had projected demand of an outlay of
Rs. 2217.56 crore for the Annual Plan 2015-16 on the basis of various activities/schemes proposed
to be taken up by the cultural organizations/divisions under the Ministry. The Ministry of Finance has
allocated a sum of Rs. 1455.00 crore for developmental activities of the Ministry of Culture for
Annual Plan 2015-16, thereby resulting in a substantial reduction vis-a-vis the projections(Rs. 762.56
crore) on account of resource constraints. The Plan allocation for 2015-16 pegged at Rs. 1455.00
crore is about 65.61% of the outlay proposed by the Ministry of Culture for the year 2015-16.
Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for this reduction in Annual Plan allocation for the
year 2015-16.
29. The Ministry has stated that reduced allocation would adversely impact on almost all sectors/
organizations/schemes of the Ministry including Archaeological Survey of India, Museums, Libraries,
Scheme of Art & Culture and Centenary Celebrations, etc. Ministry of Culture has, accordingly,
earmarked Plan funds among various cultural organizations/schemes keeping in view their minimum
requirements and overall Plan funds allocated by Ministry of Finance.
30. The financial year 2014-15, Ministry of Culture had achieved more than 50% of the total Plan
allocation. The Ministry has stated that the expenditure level was slowed down to 64% during the
period October - December, 2014 due to the proposed reduction in the allocation at the Revised
Estimates stage. As against RE 2014-15 of Rs. 1500.00 crore, Ministry of Culture has incurred Plan
expenditure of Rs. 1292.37 crore (as on 15/03/2015) during the year 2014-15 which is about 86.16
% of RE 2014-15.
31. The Committee is at a loss to note that allocations had been reduced in almost all
sectors, which has adversely impacted Archaeology, Museums, Libraries and other important
Organizations under the Ministry. Culture imparts important identity to a nation. In the
development paradigm, culture plays a crucial role in the life of a nation. Therefore,
preserving, protecting and promoting our rich cultural heritage assume greater significance,
for which the Ministry must get adequate allocation. The Committee is of the firm view that
with the existing scale of allocation, even the existing schemes and activities of the Ministry
will be difficult to run. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry
should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation at the RE stage in the current
financial year, with the Ministry of Finance.
Non-Plan
32. As regards Non-Plan funds, a sum of Rs. 714.00 crore has been provided during 2015-16 as
against Rs. 659.00 crore allocated in RE 2014-15. An amount of Rs. 714.00 crore provided in BE

8

component. Funds have been provided from the allocation under salary and non-salary components
to meet the committed liabilities such as, increased salaries, DA, Retirement Benefits, Pension,
Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP), Other Administrative Expenditure, electricity bills, etc.
of all organizations under the Ministry of Culture to the maximum extent possible. In addition to this,
Non-Plan provision for regular upkeep and maintenance for protection and conservation activities of
Archaeological Survey of India has also been kept during the year 2015-16.

34. Even the Non- Plan allocation of the Ministry, the Committee believes, does not inspire
confidence as the success of Plan activities largely depends upon the Non- Plan activities.
Existence of large number of vacancies and lack of adequate manpower at various levels
particularly in ASI, will certainly adversely affect the regular upkeep, maintenance,
protection and preservation of our cultural heritage. Pace of expenditure in this section,
Committee hopes would be maintained in future also.
Issues taken up/pending with Ministry of Finance
35. The Ministry of Culture has informed the Committee that the Ministry has taken up the issue
regarding five World Heritage Sites declared by Minister of Finance in his Budget Speech (2015), with
Ministry of Finance. Besides, a monument  viz.,  Qutub Shahi Tombs, Hyderbad (Telangana) is on the
tentative World Heritage List. ASI is responsible for the restoration, conservation, preservation and
supportive infrastructure work for these protected monuments/sites. In addition, ASI proposed to
implement a project entitled Adarsh Smarak in which 25 ASI protected monuments will be converted
into model monuments with providing all the modern facilities including audio visual guides. Ministry
of Culture has also pointed out the requirement of additional Plan funds for implementing the Dandi
Projects (Memorial and Heritage Path) announced by the Hon'ble PM on the anniversary of Dandi
March. Accordingly, Ministry of Finance has been requested to consider an additional allocation of
Rs.60.00 crore (Rs.35.00 crore for ASI protected World Heritage Sites and Rs.25.00 crore for Adarsh
Smarak Project) and Rs.60.00 crore for Dandi Memorial project during 2015-16. The Ministry has
also stated that the response in this regard is awaited from the Ministry of Finance.

9
36. The Committee notes that the sums demanded by the Ministry of Culture are required
for not only existing schemes, but also for new ones declared mid way by the Prime Minister
as well as Finance Minister. The Committee, therefore, strongly endorses the request put
forth by the Ministry to the Ministry of Finance. The Committee is of the firm view that
reduced allocation for vital Schemes of the Ministry would adversely affect the core activities
of the Ministry, thereby, undermining the mandate of the Ministry.
Savings/under-utilizations during 2014-15
37. As against total budgetary provision of Rs.2511.00 crore at BE 2014-15, it was reduced to
Rs. 2159.00 crore at RE stage 2014-15 on account of massive cut imposed by the Ministry of
Finance under Plan and Non-Plan heads. The Ministry has incurred an expenditure of Rs.1880.82
crore upto February, 2015 as against RE of Rs. 2159.00 crore during the current financial year 2015-
16. The Ministry has informed that the total expenditure level upto February, 2015 is about 87.12%
of RE 2014-15.
38. The Committee notes that as per the details furnished by the Ministry, savings during
2013-14 was due to varied reasons such as non-filling up of vacant posts, delay in completion
of works, postponement of some programmes etc.
39. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry that every possible step should be taken
to ensure that under- utilization of funds does not occur. The Committee is of the view that
periodic monitoring by the Ministry, of the progress of schemes/programmes would help in
identifying the reasons for under-utilization at an early stage and in taking remedial action.
Further, the Committee stresses upon the need for strict monitoring and supervision of the
utilization of the grants given to the Organisations under the Ministry.
40. Filling vacant posts should also be expedited or outsourcing some activities may also be
considered.
41. The Committee could understand from the Outcome Budget that under the 'Grants-in-aid' Head
of various organizations, significant amounts were surrendered to Ministry of Finance due to receipt
of less number of eligible applications.
42. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the failure in properly assessing the
prospective number of applications and why such a pattern is repeated. The Committee also
desires that the Ministry may take serious note of this and also inform the Committee about
the steps taken to reduce the Savings.
Delay in implementation of Schemes/Non-availability of grants
43. The Committee could understand from the Outcome Budget of the Ministry that the scheme
'Setting up of performing Arts' Centre and International Cultural Centres' is likely to be taken off
during 2015-16 and that new scheme is under process.
44. The Committee does not know the reasons for scrapping the Scheme and what are the
details of the proposed new Scheme. The Ministry may have had strong reasons to drop the
Scheme midway. Taking off a scheme and starting a new scheme leaves a time gap and we
do not get value for the public money already spent. In the instant case, the Committee would
like to know whether any evaluation of the Scheme was done and also the reasons which led
to discontinuing the Scheme.

10
45. The Ministry has stated that the Scheme 'Setting up of National/Regional School of Drama' will
be implemented only in the next financial year that could not be done in the last fiscal due to
manpower shortage.
46. The Committee is of the view that such delays indicate lack of proper planning &
management and recommends that steps be taken in advance to obviate such avoidable delays
as existence of vacancy is not an unforeseen problem.
47. The Ministry, in its Outcome Budget, has stated that the 'Scheme for Support to State
Akademis' is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for rejuvenating the Sate Akademis working in the field
of performing, visual and literary arts by giving assistance in each State on the basis of Annual action
plan to be drawn up by the State Akademis. However, the Committee notes that this scheme could
not be taken up for implementation during the 12th Plan period on account of downsizing.
48. Taking into account the poor financial condition of the State Akademis, the Committee
feels that Central assistance could have helped a great deal in revitalizing them. The
Committee, therefore, is of the view that the Ministry should explore the possibilities of
implementing this Plan Scheme. The Committee also recommends the Ministry to take up the
matter with Ministry of Finance to get Plan assistance for  State Akademis.
49. The Committee understands that the funding from the Ministry of Culture to 'Institutions &
Individuals engaged in Literary Activities' was stopped from 2013-14 onwards. Earlier, a regular
annual grant was provided to these Organisations.
50. The Ministry has stated in its Outcome Budget that under the 'Capacity Building and Training
Scheme for Museum Professionals', in-service training to Museum staff to create a dedicated cadre
of experts, museum professional will be undertaken. The Ministry also stated that during 2013-14,
under the 'Financial Assistance for Promotion of Art & Culture', no fund was released to engage
leading professional agencies to study the system in place and then develop online application.
Besides, no grant was released upto March 2014 to set up a co-ordination mechanism on Intangible
Cultural Heritage.
51. The Committee would like to know the reasons for the discontinuance of the funding
of the above said Schemes and also its likely impact in the promotion of literary activities.
52. The Committee feels that such an initiative would have enabled the use of complete
online system for releasing grants in the Ministry, which would have brought in more
transparency in the process. The Committee, therefore, recommends that this important
component of the scheme should be given urgent attention.
53. The Committee may also be apprised of the reasons for discontinuing the Ministry's funding
given to the Institute of Historical Studies, Kolkata and Numismatic Society of India, Varanasi.
Audit Paras
54. The Committee takes serious note of the extension of undue benefits in terms of money
and extension of services to the staff of the Asiatic Society, Kolkata and extension of services
of staff of National School of Drama. The Committee is unhappy to note the blocking of
capital in respect of the Guest House of IGNCA. It would like to know the status in these
regards.
55. The Committee was informed that the land allotted in the year 2000 for the construction of

11
Institute of Archaeology at Greater Noida Authority and imposed a huge amount as fine on the
Ministry of Culture. The Ministry could not undertake construction during all these years due to one
or the other reason which led to the cancellation of the land allotment.
56. The Committee views the cancellation of land allotment due to non-construction very
seriously; it is an example of stark inefficiency , carelessness and bur eaucratic lethargy. When
asked, the Committee was not given any convincing reason for this. It, therefore,
recommends that appropriate measures may be taken to fix responsibility for the delay and
those responsible be taken to task, as it had led to loss of crores of public money.
57. The Committee strongly recommends that stringent and periodic monitoring of the
various Organisations under the Ministry should be done in order to avoid such serious
discrepancies. The Committee also emphasizes the need for strict adherence to well
established financial and administrative guidelines.
Archaeological Survey of India
58. The major activities of the Archaeological Survey of India are:
1. Survey of archaeological remains and excavations;
2. Maintenance and conservation of centrally protected monuments, sites and remains;
3. Chemical preservation of monuments and antiquarian remains;
4. Architectural survey of temples and secular buildings;
5. Establishment, Maintenance and running of Archaeological museums;
6. Development of epigraphical research and numismatic studies;
7. Expeditions abroad;
8. Training in Archaeology; and
9. Publication of technical reports and research work.
59. The Committee notes that the Archaeological Survey of India created three new Circles in
2013- 14 at Nagpur, Jodhpur and Sarnath by splitting Aurangabad, Jaipur, Patna and Lucknow
Circles.
60. Under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958, the ASI has
3685 protected monuments and archaeological sites of national importance in the country which
includes 21 cultural sites inscribed in the World Heritage List by UNESCO.
61. The Committee could gather from the Annual Report (2014-15) of the Ministry that digitization
work using Jatan software program is under consideration at 7 more archaeological site museums of
ASI.
62. The Committee hopes that the digitization work would be taken up in 2015-16.
Electronic Ticketing
63. The Ministry has stated that in order to facilitiate ticketing for tourists, national and
international, to all ASI ticketed monuments, ASI has introduced Electronic Ticketing, on proof of

12
concept basis, at Taj Mahal, Agra and Humayun's Tomb, Delhi. The facility will be extended to all
ASI ticketed monuments in due course.
64. The Committee hopes that e-ticketing would enable the visitors to plan their visit to the
monuments in advance and help them to avoid the hassle of waiting at the ticket counters.
This would encourage more people to visit these monuments. The Committee desires that the
process of extending this facility to all ASI ticketed monuments should be done in a time
bound manner.
E-Governance
65. The Ministry has stated that ASI has undertaken to implement e-governance in all its offices
in the country. This would entail computerization of all processes and documentation in ASI. It would
also provide online inter-face between ASI Headquarter and its field offices with the public through
digitized forms and applications.
66. The Committee appreciates this initiative of ASI.
Adarsh Smarak
67. As per the Annual Report of the Ministry, ASI has identified 25 monuments which would be
upgraded in first phase as Adarsh Smarak. Each Adarsh Smarak would offer enhanced security,
improved signage, aids for differently abled such as brail, Wi-Fi, water management facilities amongst
other things to the tourists.
68. The Committee had in its previous Reports recommended for improved facilities for the
visitors at the ASI monuments. The Committee hopes that this project would improve the
upkeep of these monuments considerably. The Committee desires that all the ASI monuments
should be upgraded to the standards of the Adarsh Smarak in a phased manner.
Encroachment of Monuments
69. The Committee appreciates the significant role played by ASI in protecting the monuments and
heritage sites of our country. It is an undisputed fact that the encroachment of ASI protected
monuments can be prevented only by better co-ordination with and co-operation from State
Governments.
70. The Ministry, in its reply, has stated that the Secretary (Culture) has written to the Chief
Secretaries of all State Governments/ Union Territories requesting formation of State level Co-
ordination Committees in this regard and that positive response has been received from four State
Governments.
71. The Secretary, while making a presentation before the Committee, stated that Jammu& Kashmir
Government has recently constituted State level Co-ordination Committee.
72. In addition to the 3685 Centrally protected monuments, there are large number of monuments
of archaeological value under the control of the State Governments.
73. The Ministry, in its reply furnished to the Committee, has stated that the monuments under the
jurisdiction of respective States are taken care of by the Archaeology Departments of the concerned
State. The budgetary allocation is made for conservation/preservation of the State protected
monuments by the concerned State Governments. Any technical help requested by the State

13
Governments for conservation work of the monuments is provided by the Archaeological Survey of
India. In some cases where the request is received for conservation work of State protected
monuments on Deposit Work basis, the ASI takes up necessary execution of the work on deposit of
the funds by the State Governments.
74. The Committee emphasizes the need for greater co-ordination between ASI, State
Governments and the local authorities in the matter of prevention and removal of
encroachments at our monuments. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry to
aggressively pursue the matter of setting up the State level Co-ordination Committees, with
the remaining State Governments.
75. The Committee also urges that the field offices of ASI should pursue such cases of
encroachment persistently with the District Authorities on urgent basis and chalk a way out
in such cases. The Committee also underlines the need for adequate follow up of the cases
filed in Court of law against the encroachers.
76. As a preventive measure, the Committee likes the Ministry to consider the idea of
having a Central Force specially for protecting/ guarding our cultural heritage sites/
monuments on the lines of CISF and BSF etc. It can be' utilized both for Central and State
sites.
77. The Committee is unhappy to note that even though ASI issued 1950 demolition orders during
the last 4 years, only 32 such orders were executed. The Ministry's reply states that the
implementation of the demolition orders issued under Section 38(1) and 38 (2) of the Ancient
Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act by the Director General of ASI is a
responsibility of the District Administration.
78. The Committee understands the difficulties faced by ASI in this regard. The Committee is also
aware that there are a number of Court cases against the demolition orders issued by ASI.
79. In this regard, the Committee is of the view that ASI can fulfill its mandate only when
it has an adequate statutory backing to tackle encroachments. The Committee notes that at
present, ASI does not have inherent powers to execute the demolition orders issued by it.
Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that adequate powers should be granted to
ASI under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 which
would equip ASI to execute its demolition orders. The Committee is also of the considered
view that the Act should stipulate the action that can be taken against the District Authorities
in case of laxity or non-co-operation on their part in executing the demolition orders.
80. The Committee also recommends that a Task Force may be constituted in the States
wherein encroachment of monuments situated in communally sensitive areas are to be
removed. The specialized Task Force can co-ordinate with the District Authorities and the ASI
to remove the encroachers.
81. The Committee feels that keeping in view the humanitarian aspect of encroachments,
creation of a separate fund for removing of illegal encroachment & for rehabilitation would
ensure that the monument is protected and also that the encroachers are suitably
rehabilitated, without adversely affecting their lives. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
earlier recommendation that a separate fund is needed for removing of illegal encroachments
and for rehabilitation.

14
82. The Secretary informed the Committee that the ASI has made an assessment of a requirement
of sum of Rs.200 crores approximately for construction/repairs of nearly 250 kms. of perimeter of
masonry/grill fencing. However, a proposal of Rs.100 crores for construction of perimeter walls was
not acceded to by the Ministry of Finance.
83. The Committee is of the view that the demand made by ASI is justified and essential
for the upkeep of monuments and heritage sites. Therefore, the Committee endorses this
demand and desires that the Ministry may pursue this demand vigorously.
84. The Secretary apprised the Committee that a conservation policy and an excavation policy have
been notified and that the guidelines on notification and de-notification of monuments have been
drafted and uploaded on the website.
85. The Committee appreciates this initiative.
86. The Committee was informed by the Secretary that the Committee which was set up to
recommend the manpower and infrastructure to be created for provisioning security of our
monuments has recommended engagement of additional 7000 security guards for the monuments.
87. The Committee notes that if a monument of archeological or heritage value is lost, it
is lost forever. Therefor e, it is essential that we should take every effort to protect it. The
Committee, accordingly, recommends that the Ministry should ensure that adequate number
of security personnel should be provided for the safety and security of the monuments.
National Culture Fund
88. The National Culture Fund was established by the Government of India (Ministry of Culture)
as a trust vide notification published in the Gazette of India of 28th November, 1996.
89. As per the reply furnished by the Ministry, Ministry of Culture had vigorously pursued the
matter of including "Culture and Heritage" in the lists of items for which Corporate Social
Responsibility Funds would be utilised. As a result thereof, Corporates can now fund projects
pertaining to Culture and heritage under their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) obligations, as
enunciated in item 1 (v) of Schedule VII of the Corporate Act 2013, as well as the provisions of the
Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014. These came into effect from April 1, 2014.
90. The Ministry has informed that ASI has partnered with several PSUs for funding of
conservation works as well as for providing visitors amenities at selected important monuments
including World Heritage sites. 25 proposals from 12 Circles worth nearly Rs.150 crores have been
forwarded to NCF for funding for providing visitors amenities as well as conservation.
91. The Committee notes the achievement of the Ministry. The Committee is happy to note
that the NCF could attract corporate interest in preserving and promoting our culture and
heritage. The Committee feels that more corporates need to be encouraged to come forward
to become stakeholders in the NCF and the Ministry should actively take initiative in this
regard. It has since been included as an allowed activity under CSR also.

Akademi and Lalit Kala Akademi.

'Festival of Letters' called Face to Face programme was introduced this year, where Award winning
writers were face to face with the reader, being in discussion with the critic and readers.
94. The Committee appreciates this initiative and hopes that this programme would help in
enabling an active interface between the writers, critics and readers.

look into various issues related to Akademis submitted its Report in May 2014 and that the HPC has
advised that a Committee be set up to implement the recommendations. The Ministry, in its reply, has
informed the Committee that the recommendations made by the High Powered Committee have been
analyzed in consultation with the Akademies / Organizations concerned, under the Ministry of Culture
and a proposal incorporating the HPC recommendations, views of the organizations concerned and
the observations of the Ministry of Culture thereon, is presently under consideration of the Ministry.

implemented. The Committee hopes that the implementation of these recommendations would

creation of a separate Akademi for "Tribal and Folk Arts" should be seriously considered.

National Mission on Libraries
102. The National Mission on Libraries was constituted on 4 May, 2012 to revamp and develop
Library & Information Science sector in the country.

16
103. As per the information furnished by the Ministry, the NML has so far held seven meetings. It
established four working groups to draw a programme to develop the Libraries & Information
Science sector in the country. After deliberating on the recommendations of the working groups and
on the basis of the recommendations of the working groups, NML formulated a plan scheme:
"National Mission on Libraries-Up gradation of Libraries providing services to the Public".
104. The main features of the scheme are (a) Creation of National Virtual Library of India; (b)
Setting up of NML Model Libraries; (c) Quantitative & Qualitative Survey of Libraries; and (d)
Capacity Building. The scheme also envisaged setting up a Project Management Unit for
implementation of the scheme. The scheme was approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs
on 28.11.2013 with a plan outlay of ` 400.00 Crore for the twelfth plan period.
105. The Ministry has informed that for Creation of National Virtual Library of India, Expression of
Interest and Request for Qualification were called for and the responses received are being scrutinized
to shortlist the agencies. The Request for Proposal to the shortlisted agencies would be issued in due
course.
106. The Committee endorses the importance of creation of National Virtual Library. The
Committee desires that the Ministry should closely monitor the process of creation of
National Virtual Library and ensure timely completion thereof.
National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities
107. National Mission On Monuments And Antiquities was initially approved for a period of 5 years
i.e. 2007 - 2012 in the XI five year plan with the objective to prepare a National database on Built
Heritage and sites from secondary sources and a National database on Antiquities from different
sources and museums. To sustain the momentum and to complete the remaining documentation work,
the Standing Finance Committee (SFC) recommended its extension as a Central Scheme with certain
modifications (introduction of primary survey of built heritage and sites, strengthening infrastructure
etc.) under XII five year plan (2012 - 2017) with a budgetary outlay of ` 99.20 crore in April 2013.
108. The Committee hopes that the expected output of the Mission viz., National Register on
Built Heritage & Sites, National Register on Antiquities and Publication & Publicity would be
achieved in due course.

109. National Council of Science Museums(NCSM), an autonomous organization under the Ministry

Science Outreach programmes such as Science Seminar, Science Drama, Science & Engineering Fair,
Science Film Festival, Workshops, Training, Lectures and Science demonstrations etc. for general
public and students in particular.
110. The Committee acknowledges the crucial role played by the Science Museums in

Buddhist Circuit
130. The Committee was informed that the Ministry of Tourism has identified three circuit - two
site-wise and one State-wise to be developed as integrated Buddhist Circuits in the country, with the
help of Central Government/State Government/private Stakeholders for the convenience of the
tourists/visitors.
131. The Committee also finds a distinct lack of co-ordination among the concerned Union
Ministries viz., Culture, Tourism, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways and that the

regard should be chalked out without further delay. The Committee also urges the Ministry
to have a formal mechanism to have an effective co-ordination among the Ministry of Culture
and Archaeological Survey of India, Ministries of Tourism, Civil Aviation, Road Transport &
Highways and the respective State Governments to ensure that all the Buddhist places are
integrated seamlessly, well connected by good roads, transportation, airports, safety, security
etc. so that Buddhist tourists are attracted to come in large numbers who are not coming now
mainly because we do not have these facilities. It will earn enough respect as also revenue
for us, apart from commercial benefits to the stakeholders, big and small.

OBSERV ATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE — AT A GLANCE
Assessment of the Demands for Grants (2015-16) of the Ministry
The Committee notes that the present Budget Estimates shows an increase of just Rs.10
crores in comparison to the Revised Estimate last year i.e., 2014-15. The Committee is also
surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a sharp budgetary cut at RE stage in the last
financial year. The Committee failed to get a convincing reason for this cut. Given the
importance of the mandate of this Ministry i.e., to preserve, protect and promote our vast
cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible, spread across the length and breadth of the
country, the Committee is at a loss to see that Plan allocation to this Ministry has come down
from Rs.1835 crore in BE 2014-15 to Rs.1500 crore in RE 2014-15 and to Rs.1455 crore in BE
of 2015-16. Such allocation are highly insufficient and the Committee recommends that Plan
allocation for the Department be increased adequately at RE stage. (Para 13)
Twelfth Five Year Plan
The Committee notes that against the proposed outlay of Rs.18608.94 crore, only
Rs.7275.00 crore were earmarked for the Twelfth Five Year Plan. Due to this severe
downsizing, many important Schemes mentioned above, could not be taken up by the Ministry.
Since three years of the plan period have been over, the Committee recommends that for the
remaining two years, the Plan allocation for the Ministry of Culture should be hiked so that
important schemes/projects should not suffer. The Committee also would like to know the
rationale for abandoning the three schemes in the Museum Sector by the Ministry along with
an impact-assessment Report. (Para 16)
Spending pattern during the Twelfth Plan
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry was able to spend more than 90%
of its allocation during the first three years of the Twelfth Plan. At the same time, the
Committee observes that better planning and supervision could have definitely improved the
pace of utilization. (Para 20)
2015-16
The Committee notes that the group- wise allocation will help the Ministry to reallocate
funds among the Schemes subsumed within the group, when the need arises. The Committee
hopes that this financial arrangement would impart more flexibility to the Ministry in terms
of allocation, leading to optimum utilization of funds. Nevertheless, the Committee desires
that due care and caution should be exercised to ensure that the new scheme of allocation
does not affect the progress of existing schemes/ programmes of the Ministry and also the
functioning of vital Organisations under the Ministry. The Committee would like to emphasize
that the interse fund allocation of the grouped heads should be brought to the notice of the
Committee at appropriate time. (Para 27)
23

24
Ministry's Projected Demand vis-a-vis Budgetary allocation
The Committee is at a loss to note that allocations had been reduced in almost all
sectors, which has adversely impacted Archaeology, Museums, Libraries and other important
Organizations under the Ministry. Culture imparts important identity to a nation. In the
development paradigm, culture plays a crucial role in the life of a nation. Therefore,
preserving, protecting and promoting our rich cultural heritage assume greater significance,
for which the Ministry must get adequate allocation. The Committee is of the firm view that
with the existing scale of allocation, even the existing schemes and activities of the Ministry
will be difficult to run. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that the Ministry
should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation at the RE stage in the current
financial year, with the Ministry of Finance. (Para 31)
Non-Plan
Even the Non- Plan allocation of the Ministry, the Committee believes, does not inspire
confidence as the success of Plan activities largely depends upon the Non- Plan activities.
Existence of large number of vacancies and lack of adequate manpower at various levels
particularly in ASI, will certainly adversely affect the regular upkeep, maintenance,
protection and preservation of our cultural heritage. Pace of expenditure in this section,
Committee hopes would be maintained in future also. (Para 34)
Issues Taken up/pending with Ministry of Finance
The Committee notes that the sums demanded by the Ministry of Culture are required
for not only existing schemes, but also for new ones declared mid way by the Prime Minister
as well as Finance Minister. The Committee, therefore, strongly endorses the request put
forth by the Ministry to the Ministry of Finance. The Committee is of the firm view that
reduced allocation for vital Schemes of the Ministry would adversely affect the core activities
of the Ministry, thereby, undermining the mandate of the Ministry. (Para 36)
Savings/ under-utilizations during 2014-15
The Committee notes that as per the details furnished by the Ministry, savings during
2013-14 was due to varied reasons such as non-filling up of vacant posts, delay in completion
of works, postponement of some programmes etc. (Para 38)
The Committee impresses upon the Ministry that every possible step should be taken
to ensure that under-utilization of funds does not occur. The Committee is of the view that
periodic monitoring by the Ministry, of the progress of schemes/programmes would help in
identifying the reasons for under-utilization at an early stage and in taking remedial action.
Further, the Committee stresses upon the need for strict monitoring and supervision of the
utilization of the grants given to the Organisations under the Ministry. (Para 39)
Filling vacant posts should also be expedited or outsourcing some activities may also be
considered. (Para 40)
The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the failure in properly assessing the
prospective number of applications and why such a pattern is repeated. The Committee also
desires that the Ministry may take serious note of this and also inform the Committee about
the steps taken to reduce the Savings. (Para 42)

25
Delay in implementation of Schemes/Non-availability of grants
The Committee does not know the reasons for scrapping the Scheme and what are the
details of the proposed new Scheme. The Ministry may have had strong reasons to drop the
Scheme midway. Taking off a scheme and starting a new scheme leaves a time gap and we
do not get value for the public money already spent. In the instant case, the Committee would
like to know whether any evaluation of the Scheme was done and also the reasons which led
to discontinuing the Scheme. (Para 44)
The Committee is of the view that such delays indicate lack of proper planning and
management and recommends that steps be taken in advance to obviate such avoidable delays
as existence of vacancy is not an unforeseen problem. (Para 46)
Taking into account the poor financial condition of the State Akademis, the Committee
feels that Central assistance could have helped a great deal in revitalizing them. The
Committee, therefore, is of the view that the Ministry should explore the possibilities of
implementing this Plan Scheme. The Committee also recommends the Ministry to take up the
matter with Ministry of Finance to get Plan assistance for  State Akademis. (Para 48)
The Committee would like to know the reasons for the discontinuance of the funding
of the above said Schemes and also its likely impact in the promotion of literary activities.
(Para 51)
The Committee feels that such an initiative would have enabled the use of complete
online system for releasing grants in the Ministry, which would have brought in more
transparency in the process. The Committee, therefore, recommends that this important
component of the scheme should be given urgent attention. (Para 52)
The Committee may also be apprised of the reasons for discontinuing the Ministry's
funding given to the Institute of Historical Studies, Kolkata and Numismatic Society of India,
Varanasi. (Para 53)
Audit Paras
The Committee takes serious note of the extension of undue benefits in terms of money
and extension of services to the staff of the Asiatic Society, Kolkata and extension of services
of staff of National School of Drama. The Committee is unhappy to note the blocking of
capital in respect of the Guest House of IGNCA. It would like to know the status in these
regards. (Para 54)
The Committee views the cancellation of land allotment due to non-construction very
seriously; it is an example of stark inefficiency , carelessness and bur eaucratic lethargy. When
asked, the Committee was not given any convincing reason for this. It, therefore,
recommends that appropriate measures may be taken to fix responsibility for the delay and
those responsible be taken to task, as it had led to loss of crores of public money.
(Para 56)
The Committee strongly recommends that stringent and periodic monitoring of the
various Organisations under the Ministry should be done in order to avoid such serious
discrepancies. The Committee also emphasizes the need for strict adherence to well
established financial and administrative guidelines. (Para 57)

26
Archaeological Survey of India
The Committee hopes that the digitization work would be taken up in 2015-16.
(Para 62)
Electronic Ticketing
The Committee hopes that e-ticketing would enable the visitors to plan their visit to the
monuments in advance and help them to avoid the hassle of waiting at the ticket counters.
This would encourage more people to visit these monuments. The Committee desires that the
process of extending this facility to all ASI ticketed monuments should be done in a time
bound manner. (Para 64)
E-Governance
The Committee appreciates this initiative of ASI. (Para 66)
Adarsh Smarak
The Committee had in its previous Reports recommended for improved facilities for the
visitors at the ASI monuments. The Committee hopes that this project would improve the
upkeep of these monuments considerably. The Committee desires that all the ASI monuments
should be upgraded to the standards of the Adarsh Smarak in a phased manner.  (Para 68)
Encroachment of Monuments
The Committee emphasizes the need for greater co-ordination between ASI, State
Governments and the local authorities in the matter of prevention and removal of
encroachments at our monuments. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry to
aggressively pursue the matter of setting up the State level Co-ordination Committees, with
the remaining State Governments. (Para 74)
The Committee also urges that the field offices of ASI should pursue such cases of
encroachment persistently with the District Authorities on urgent basis and chalk a way out
in such cases. The Committee also underlines the need for adequate follow up of the cases
filed in court of law against the encroachers. (Para 75)
As a preventive measure, the Committee likes the Ministry to consider the idea of
having a Central Force specially for protecting/ guarding our cultural heritage sites/
monuments on the lines of CISF and BSF etc. It can be utilized both for Central and State
sites. (Para 76)
In this regard, the Committee is of the view that ASI can fulfill its mandate only
when it has an adequate statutory backing to tackle encroachments. The Committee
notes that at present, ASI does not have inherent powers to execute the demolition orders
issued by it. Therefore, the Committee strongly recommends that adequate powers should be
granted to ASI under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958
which would equip ASI to execute its demolition orders. The Committee is also of the
considered view that the Act should stipulate the action that can be taken against the District

27
Authorities in case of laxity or non-co-operation on their part in executing the demolition
orders. (Para 79)
The Committee also recommends that a Task Force may be constituted in the States
wherein encroachment of monuments situated in communally sensitive areas are to be
removed. The specialized Task Force can co-ordinate with the District Authorities and the ASI
to remove the encroachers. (Para 80)
The Committee feels that keeping in view the humanitarian aspect of encroachments,
creation of a separate fund for removing of illegal encroachment and for rehabilitation would
ensure that the monument is protected and also that the encroachers are suitably
rehabilitated, without adversely affecting their lives. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
earlier recommendation that a separate fund is needed for removing of illegal encroachments
and for rehabilitation. (Para 81)
The Committee is of the view that the demand made by ASI is justified and essential
for the upkeep of monuments and heritage sites. Therefore, the Committee endorses this
demand and desires that the Ministry may pursue this demand vigorously. (Para 83)
The Committee appreciates this initiative. (Para 85)
The Committee notes that if a monument of archeological or heritage value is lost, it
is lost forever. Therefore, it is essential that we should take every effort to protect it. The
Committee, accordingly, recommends that the Ministry should ensure that adequate number
of security personnel should be provided for the safety and security of the monuments.
(Para 87)

Airpor ts Authority of India (A .A.l .) for civil aviation purposes . These enclaves, co nsist of

not interfere with the operational and security requirements of the defence airfields within 
which they are located .. Such enclaves were created at these 28 airfields, as no separate civil 
airport/ infrastructure was considered feasible at that statio n because of the land intensive 
and cost intensive nature of deve lopment, aodl also because these did not lend themselves to 
regulatory requirements of air space, given the existence of the defe nce airfields. The No

2. Not all lbe 28 airfields were originally oonstructed for defence purposes. Six of these 
viz., Bbuj, Bagdogn, Vi.ba!cbapatnam, Silcbar, Port Blair and Gwalior were initially civil 
airports, but were Jatu oouverted into defence airfields.

3. The Department of Civil Aviation in their note submitted to the Committee bas 
stated that the civil enclaves operate under a number of constraints which may be 
summarised tts under:-
(a) Owing to sbonage of space at almost all defence airpons where civil enclaves are 
operating , a lim.ited area has been given for creating civil infrastructure . 
Expansion I modification of already created terminal buildings poses considerable 
problems, since there is no additional space available for modular expansion. 
(b) Because of space constraints, AAJ is unable to create cargo/ commercial 
infrastructure. 
(c) Air Traffic control is managed by the defence authorities on these airfields. 
Therefore, the entire watch-hour is dependent upon the requirements of defence 
force. 
(d) Time slots for the civil aviation is dictat ed by the defence requirements and civil 
aviation has to accept this constraint. In most cases, defence has been very 
cooperative in their endeavour to care to civil requirements. 
(e) The radio navigational aids, lighting system, etc. provided at defence airfields are 
commensurate with the defence requirements and their operational standards. 
However, these mostly fall below ICAO norms. AAJ bas therefore to provide 
these facilities at their expense. 
(f) Given defence requirements , often, expansion of watch hours becomes a great 
problem. 
(g) The radio navigational aids provided by the AA1 have to be serviced and 
maintained. While doing so, technical personnel have to face some problems on 
account of security constraints. 
(h) Despite heavy investments by the AAI in the defence airfields, returns to them are 
negligible, as air traflic control is handled by defence authorities and the tanding 
fee is collected by the de'fence authorities and deposited in the Consolidated Fund 
of India. 
(i) Power supply at defence airfields, at times, is not sufficient to cater to the needs of 
the civil enclave. Wherever possible, AAI has created independent power sources 
to cater to its own needs. 
(j) Administration and Coordination : The command and control of the defence 
airports are under their respective commanders. Control over civil enclave,s is 
exercised by the Airport Directors nominated by AAl. The latter have been 
advised, and maintain very close administrative coordination with the defence 
commanders in all matters. Usually all help is provided by the defence 
commanders. 
(k) Legal problems : Any dispute over land or legal requiremenu are referred to AAl 
Headquarters who in turn take it up with Defence Headquarters for their 
indulgenc~ and help. Most of the difficulties are sorted out through coordination 
meetings at appropriate levels with mutual cooperation. 
4. The Conimittee at its meeting held on the 20th February. 1996 heard the views of the 
Secretary, Department of Civil Aviation, and also the Defence Secretary in the matter . 
. )YJ!jler.deposing before the Gornrnittee, Secretary. Department of Civil Aviation has stated 
miiJ tJi.e problep~s at these c!,yil enclaves have incrl}a.SC#, during> ~e, last fiv~ years a~ th~re has 
been rapid growth in air traffic. The COI\~trairlts have been . felt more at such places C!.S

Bangalore, Goa, Pune and Cochin. When aslced about the long term plans/scientific studies 
for these civil enclaves, the Secretary informed the Committee that there were no such long 
term plans for the development of these enclaves. However, Department of Civil Aviation 
has identified plans for new airports keeping in view growing traffic requirements. Airports 
at Cochin, Bangalore and Goa have been given top priority. Separate airports at Cochin and 
Bangalore are being set up. An alternative site for new airport at Goa is yet to be identified. 
There are seven airports viz., Jodhpur, Pune, Agra, Allahabad, Chandigarh, Bagdogra and 
Gwalior which would acquire importance within the next five years or so and problems in 
these airports are proposed tO be tackled in a similar manner. 
5. As regards the investment made by the Airport Authority of India, the Committee 
has been informed by the Secretary that so far an investment of Rs. 251 crores has been 
made in these civil enclaves. This includes expenditure on (i) aerodrom works such as 
pavements, terminal and ancillary buildings, (ii) navigational aids and (iii) ground safety 
services. The revenue from these enclaves was however not commensurate with the 
investment made therein . Sources of revenue earning from these enclaves include Radio 
Navigational Facility Charges (RNFC) and non-traffic revenue. The major chunk of revenue 
i.e. landing charges collected ther efrom goes. to the Consolidated Fund of India and is then 
allocated to defence in the following year. The revenue so collected does not come back to 
the Airport Authority for investment in the development of aviation infrastructure. The AAl 
also does not get budgetary support from the Government. 
6. The Committe e has been informed by the Secretary that these enclave s also face 
severe constraints on account of shor tages of space which does not allow them to create 
additional cargo I commercial infrastructure and instal navigational aids such as DVOR ILS 
ere. Consequently, these enclaves do not meet lCAO specifications for civil operations. The 
maintenance staff at times is also not allowed to maintain the facilities. 
7. The Committee was .informed that Air Traffic Control (ATC) watch hours of defence 
airfields are controlled by the Defence For\OCS according to their own requirements. The civil 
flights are by and large restricted between 10.00 a.m. to 8.00 p.m. and not adjusted in case 
of delay due to bad weather or technical reasons. 
8. The Committee also heard the Defence Secretary on the matter. The Defence 
Secretary informed the Committee that there had been maximum possible cooperation from 
their side to accommodating civi.l aviation operation at these civil enclaves . On being asked 
whether Ministry of Defence have ever given a thought about separating civil enclaves from 
defence airfields or shifting of some of their airfields which are located in the cities, the 
Defence Secretary informed the Committee that keeping in view the high use of these 
airports, separate airfields at Goa (international) & Agra are under consideration. A 
Committee has been set up to examine the issue and the report is expected very shortly. As 
regards the shifting of defence airfields fro m its existing location, the Secretary stated that 
location of an airfield is important from the point of view of the operational plans of the 
armed forces. 
Recommendations 
9. The Committee noted the const raints being faced by the Department .of Civil 
Aviation at the Civil enclaves in the defence airfields. These constraints have adversely 
affected the operation of civil flights during the last 4-5 years due to the considerable 
increase in air traffic. Th~ 'problem has been more acute particularly at the places such as 
Bangalore, Cochin, Goa and. Agra wherc; .,~xpansion of infrastructural facilities is needed, 
given the tourist as well as commercial traffic. These places are now attracting more 
international Oighl$. The Committee has noted that there has been full cooperation from the 

4 
Defence authorities in the matter of civil aviation at the existing airports, and beyond that it 
does not seem feasible for the defence to serve the operation al com mitm ents of the civil 
authoritie s. The ColllDllttee, theref ore, recommend s that some altogether separate places for 
civil airports be provided to meet the growing demands or civil aviation. 
10. The Com mittee notes that Department of Civil Aviat ion is developing the 
infrastructure to meet ICAO specifications but the results are far from satisfactory owing to 
restrictions on the civil enclaves in the defence airfields. The Comminee is, however, 
astonished 1.0 note that the Department of Civil Avi ntion & Airports Authority of Indi a have 
not carried out any long term ~t udies on the subject of civil enclaves, their future 
requi rement, the need for expansion given the growing air traffi c etc. The Committee 
observes that problems arc being atte nded to on ad hoc and sho rt time basis. The Committee 
recommends that the Department of Civil Aviation and the AAI should carry out a stu dy/ 
survey to assess the futur e requirements and pr10pare a time bound action plan. 
11. The Comm illee tak es note of the fact that revenue from these civil enclaves is very 
low comparing the expenditure incurred on these civil enclaves by the Airport Authority of 
India. A large portion of reve nue at an airport com es from lhe landing charg es collec ted by 
the Airp ort Authori ty. In the C<Jse of civil enclaves, landing charg es are collected by the 
Defence authorities and deposited in the Consolidated Fund of India. It has been the 
considered opinion of the Commiu cc that reve nu e generated from the civil aviation sector 
be recycled for the development of aviation infrastruct ure. The Comm ittee in its 91h and 
14th Reports on the Demands Cor Grants for 1994-95 and 1995-96 respectively while 
examining the matter regarding recycling of Inland Air Travel Tax (IATI) and Foreign 
Trave l Tux (FIT) had recommende d that proceeds (rom these taxes be recycled for the 
development of aviat ion infrastructure as that would create more business which would 
ultimately lead to a higher collection of taxes by the Central exchequ er. The Committ ee-bad 
then desir ed that both the Ministry of Finance a nd Planning Commission should to take 
stock o( the situation and review their positions. ln their Action Taken Report , the 
Department of Civil Aviation had stated that the matte r was under consideration and a 
paper for considerat ion of Cabi nc l was in process. On the same analogy , the Committee 
observes tha t the landing fee collecte d from these enclaves be recycled for the development 
of aviation infrastructure. The Comm ittee recommends to the Gilvernment that keeping io 
view the expenditure incurrtd by the Authority , the landing charges should be cost shared by 
them with the Derence in a proportionate manner. The Committee therefore, wants the 
Ministries of Finan ce and Defence, and the Planning Com.missioo to review their policies and 
make available substantial percentage of !be landing fee for further investment in the aviation 
sector. 
12. As regards the problem$ being experience d on account of land con straints for the 
development of termin al facili tic~. constru ction and upgradation of civil aprons etc. and 
installation of navigational aids. the Comminee observes that the construc tion of separate 
civil airports in close proximit y of Defence ai rfields is cost intens ive and State Government 
may not be able to acquir e land for anoth er airport. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry of Defence should explore the pos:~ibility of providing the necessary tand to the AAI 
so that infrastructure could be developed as per the ICAO specifications for civil operation at 
these airfields. 
13. The Committee is aware that A TC watch bows at rbe defei\Cle airf&elds are controlled 
according to dc:Cence requirement~. The Committee is pleased t<1 note that the defence 

5 
autho rities extend their fullest cooperation in accommodating the civil flights. However , it is 
observed that civil flights face difficulties when the flights are delayed due to bad weather or 
for some technical reason~. At some of the places ther e is a need for availability of air space 
for the civil flights in the morning and late in evening hours. Tbe Committee, therefore , 
desires that the Ministry of Defence may look iDto tht matter and accommodate a gr~ter 
num~r of civil nights in thtse enclaves without hampering defeo~ operations. 
14. Attention of the Committee has been drawn to the fact that at Goa Airport, 
reside ntial quart ers for defenc.;e personnel have been located along the airstrip and peopl e 
oc-casionally cross the runway of the airport. At Bhuj, passengers face a lot of 
mconveniences as they have to wait at least o ne kilometre away from the Bhuj Airport. 1t 
has also been brought to the notice of the Committee that at some airports , e.g. Jorbat, 
hardly any civil aircrafts are allowed to land on account of lAF exercises. fhe Committee 
feels that there is a need of a permane.nt Central Co-«dinalioo Committee having 
representatives of the Department of Civil Aviation, Mlnbtry of Defence and others to look 
into such prob lems being faced in the operation of civil nights . The Committee desires that 
such a Comm ittee shou ld ~ constituted at the earliest.

REPORT
Roads play an important role in the infrastructure development of the country. India has a
vast road network of 48.65 km. of which the National Highways and the State Highways together
account for 2,41,178 kms. The length of National Highways network is only 96,260 kms. (at present)
constituting about 1.9% of the total road network in the country and carrying about 40 per cent of
the total traffic across the length and breadth of the country. The Ministry of Road Transport and
Highways has been entrusted primarily with the functions of construction and maintenance of
National Highways (NHs), administration of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 Central Motor Vehicles Rules
1981, National Highways Act, 1956, National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection)
Rules, 2008, formulation of broad policies relating to road transport, environmental issues, automotive
norms etc. besides making arrangements for movements of vehicular traffic with neighbouring
countries.
2. The Road Transport Wing of the Ministry is concerned with the formulation of broad policies
related to road transport besides making provisions for the movement of vehicular traffic with the
neighbouring countries. The development and maintenance of National Highways are being done on
agency basis. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), State Public Works Departments
(PWDs) and the Border Roads Organization are the main agencies. Out of the total length of
96,260 km. of National Highways, 55,904 km. is with the State Public Works Departments (State
PWDs), 32,279 km. with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), 3,866 km. with the
Border Road Organization and 1,117 km. with National Highways Infrastructure Development and
Construction Limited, balance length of 3,094 km. is yet to be entrusted to the executing agencies.
3. Demand No. 83 containing the details of budget allocations of the Ministry of Road Transport
and Highways for the financial year 2015-16 was considered by the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture at its meeting held on the 8th April, 2015.
During the meeting, the Committee heard the Secretary and other officers of the Ministry of Road
Transport and Highways. The Committee also examined other budget (2015-16) documents of the
Ministry and the reply furnished by the Ministry to the questionnaire.

8. The reasons submitted by the Ministry for under-utilization of funds under some
schemes/programmes are of routine nature. The Committee feels that proper planning, timely
monitoring and taking preventing steps anticipating the routine bottlenecks would ensure
timely completion of schemes/projects and programmes. The Committee desires that
shortcomings with regard to implementation of projects may be identified in consultation with
the stakeholders involved in road projects so that such things are not repeated in future. The
Committee hopes that the spending pattern of the Ministry will see an improvement in the
coming years.
9. The Committee finds that the Ministry was not able to utilize Rs. 22.20 crore provided
from the Central Road Fund for State roads in Delhi for the year 2014-15. Though this fund
is non-lapsable, the reasons submitted by the Ministry for non-utilization due to less number
of proposals received from the Delhi Government are not impressive. The Committee hopes
that the Ministry should impress upon the State Governments in such cases to send their
proposals in time so that the allocated funds could be spent fully.
10. To a specific query on the under-utilization of funds on some schemes, the Secretary while
tendering his evidence before the Committee, informed that the majority of expenditure is incurred
during the last quarter of the financial year, as winter months are the main months for road
construction. However, Ministry of Finance imposed restrictions for ceiling of expenditure by 33%
for the last quarter of the financial year which is a major roadblock for incurring expenditure by the
Ministry.
11. The Committee appreciates the Ministry's concern in this regard. However, the
Committee notes that the Ministry did not actively pursue the matter with the Ministry of
Finance as could be understood from the reply furnished by the Ministry to the
recommendations made by the Committee in its 193rd Report in this regard. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should pursue the issue of removal of ceiling of expenditure
for the last quarter with the Ministry of Finance vigorously. The Committee urges upon the
Ministry of Finance to consider the removal on ceiling of expenditure for road projects during
the last quarter. It will help the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to spend the
allocation fully and also to complete the projects in time without cost overrun.

24. When the Ministry was asked about the role of National Highways and Infrastructure
Development Corporation Limited (NHDICL) in developing national highways in the country, the
Committee was informed that (NHIDCL) has been created to take up the task of constructing/up-
grading/widening of Highways along the border areas of the country. It is dedicated exclusively to
the task of constructing/upgrading/widening of National Highways in parts of the country which
share international boundaries with neighboring countries in order to promote regional connectivity on
a sustainable basis. The Ministry has stated that NHAI is mandated to upgrade and strengthen National
Highways through various phases of National Highways Development Project (NHDP) across the
country. However, NHIDCL has been mandated to construct/upgrade/widening of National Highways
in parts of the country which share international boundaries with neighboring countries. There is no
duplication of authority/functions between these two entities.

45. When asked about the major initiatives taken by the Ministry in the road sector, the Committee
was informed that a Hybrid Model for the Highways Sector - Annuity Mode with Construction Period
Capital Support has been introduced during the last year. As per the model, 40% of the Total Project
cost (TPC) is to be provided by the Authority to the concessionaire during the construction period
in the form of 'Construction Support'. The 'Construction Support' is to be disbursed in five equal
installments of 8% each and the timing of each such payment shall be linked to percentage of project
cost spent by the concessionaire. The concessionaire would be required to bear the balance 60% of
the project cost through a combination of its equity contribution and debt raised from the market.
Further, the 60% of the project cost borne by the concessionaire during the construction period is
to be recovered from the Authority in terms of annuity payments spread over a period of ten/twenty
years. In addition to annuity payments, there shall be separate provisions for payment of Operation
& Maintenance (O&M) payments subject to a predetermined limit and interest on outstanding balance
also to the concessionaire. The concessionaire remains responsible for O&M of the project highway
till the expiry of the concession period. The project gets transferred to the Authority after completion
of the concession period.
46. To a specific query on the annual increase in toll and lack of publicity for such increase, the
Ministry informed that a website on Toll Information System to make available in public domain,
information of public interest concerning toll plazas on National Highways/ Expressways operating
under Ministry of Road Transport & Highways and NHAI viz., the applicable User fee rates for
various categories of vehicles on any Toll Plaza, helping road users to ascertain the exact toll amount
for a particular plaza or a select route between two locations was launched on 31.10.2014. Updated
information to public/ road users about the concessions/discounts applicable for local and frequent
users etc. on any Toll Plaza is made available. The web portal is user friendly and public can access
the information through mobile phones and SMS.
47. The Committee after scrutinizing the information provided by the Ministry, expresses
its deep concern over the functioning of NHAI and the unsatisfactory progress of development
of National Highways in the country. NHAI was able to spend Rs. 6,208 crore only out of Rs.
23691.8 crore allocated during 2014-15 at RE stage. The Committee is dismayed to note that
when the private players are withdrawing from National Highways projects due to
non-availability of equity and loan to carry forward the projects, NHAI was able to spend just
26% of the allocated fund. The Committee feels that with this spending trend, NHAI would
not be in a position to achieve its targets in the coming years.
48. The Committee finds that the performance of development of National Highways under
NHDP has not seen any remarkable improvement during the last year. Projects under NHDP
III to VII are progressing at a snail's pace and there are no takers for projects under NHDP
VI. The Committee feels that the Ministry should address the bottlenecks causing the delay
at various stages of NHDP which was once considered as an ambitious project for providing
road connectivity even to the remote places of the country.
49. The Committee finds that due to difficulties faced in the award and implementation of
project stretches, the Government had to resort to Engineering, Procurement and
Construction (EPC) mode also for the construction of National Highways apart from Public
Private Partnership (PPP) mode. The Committee notes that out of 7980 Km length of National
Highways awarded during the last year, 700 km had gone on PPP mode and the rest were
Government-funded EPC projects. The Committee hopes that NHAI will complete all the
ongoing projects within the scheduled time for better National Highways connectivity across

13
the length and breadth of the country. The Ministry is requested to submit the White Paper
prepared on the performance of PPP in road projects for Committee's consideration.

12 and NH76 was also brought before the Committee. Poor condition of NH 29-Varanasi-

NH 91-Aligarh-Kanpur, NH 87-Rampur-Rudrapur, NH 24- Bareilly-Sitapur was raised during
the meeting. The Committee would also like to know the reasons for the inordinate delay in
developing Kanpur-Lucknow National Highway. Non-completion of the small stretch between
Phulbari and Salsalabari in Siliguri was also brought to the notice of the Committee.
