The Committee notes that the allocations for Port sector was Rs. 392.40 crore, but there
was drastic cut at RE stage. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons therefor. It also
expressed concern about the pattern of allocation/expenditure in respect of Light Houses.
(Para: 7)
The Committee is concerned to note that the entire allocation for the North Eastern
Region remained unutilized. The Ministry may inform the Committee about the reasons for this
lapse. The Committee is happy to note that allocation for Inland Water Transport has been
enhanced this year but feels that it is not commensurate with the requirements for developing
inland water transport in the country. More funds should be allocated for the purpose if the
Ministry/Government wants to exploit the potential in this sector optimally. (Para: 8)
The Committee urges the Ministry to make sure that the projects which did not perform
satisfactorily during 2014-15 are given necessary attention and efforts are stepped up in order
to make up the delay. (Para: 9)
Twelfth Year Plan (2012-17)
The Committee finds that the average utilization of Plan funds at 55.45% is very low just
above the half-way mark. The Committee notes that since the starting year of the 12th Plan,
there was a consistent decline in the utilization pattern of the Plan funds by the Ministry of
Shipping. The Committee is clueless about how far the Ministry would be able to achieve its
ambitious plan for capacity addition to the Ports by 1.53 times of the existing capacity at the end
of the Twelfth Plan period. The table also reflects that even Non-Plan expenditure has registered
drastic variations. (Para: 12)
The Committee feels that the Ministry of Shipping apparently failed either to plan properly
or to execute the projects which resulted in the non-utilization of 45% of the allocated funds.
The Committee desires that the Ministry should take all steps to improve the pace of utilization
of Plan and Non-Plan funds. The Committee also recommends to do a thorough analysis of the
existing bottlenecks and the reasons for this and to take corrective measures at the earliest. The
Committee may be apprised of the details of the steps taken in this regard. (Para: 13)
The Committee notes from the comparison of allocations that right from the 5th Plan to
11th Plan, water transport continued to be neglected. It has got only symbolic allocations during
the above cited Plan period. The Committee observes that keeping in view the vast potential and
long tradition of water transport including 7500 km coast line, it is high time our focus is
attracted towards this mode of transportation, which is cheaper, hassle-fr ee and environment
friendly, compared to other modes of transportation. Existing national waterways need to be
developed and put into operation as early as possible by providing required resources for this
purpose. (Para: 15)
33

34
The Committee notes that even though there was cut at the RE stage for the IWT sector,
their spending stands at Rs.118.76 crore against allocation of Rs. 76.98 crore at the RE stage.
This shows that IWT has managed to complete many proposed projects by the end of the target
period. (Para: 16)
Analysis of Annual Plan 2014-15
The Committee notes with concern the surrender/ under-utilization of allocations due to
non-finalization of some of its schemes. Such a situation does not reflect positively on the
working of those responsible/involved in implementing the schemes. (Para: 19)
There was a delay in getting environmental clearance for capital dredging work at the V .O.
Chidambarnar Port. The Committee does not approve of this and recommends that the Ministry
should ensure that in future, surrendering of major allocations should be avoided and all out
efforts be made to ensure that the Ministry does not have to surrender the allocation.
(Para: 20)
The Committee notes that there has been 37.5% cut in the allocations made, as compared
to the projected demand of the Ministry during 2015-16. The Committee desires that the Ministry
may take up this matter with the Ministry of Finance to allocate additional funds for it at
appropriate stage. (Para: 23)
Annual Plan 2015-16
The Committee finds that the Ministry is facing problems in providing a boost to the
coastal shipping project as well as repaying the pending dues of cash strapped Dredging Corporation
of India. Also, the Port sector has less allocations in 2015-16 compared to BE of 2014-15. The
Committee, therefore, recommends for allocation of more funds to the Ministry so that they may
be able to execute the capacity addition plans and expansion of water transport sector. The
Committee also recommends that DCI should be paid the amount due from the Ministry of
Shipping without any delay. (Para: 25)
Port Sector
The Committee takes serious note of the fact that many of the Major Ports have been
neglected during the budget allocations. Some of the cash strapped Ports like Kolkata Port,
Haldia Dock Complex and New Mangalore Port, have no allocation during 2015-16. The allocations
made to Cochin Port, Chennai Port and Mormugao Port are also negligible. The Committee feels
that this neglect would aggravate the already worsened financial situation of these Ports. Since
capital dredging and maintenance dredging are very essential for Port operation, especially for
the riverine Ports like Kolkata and Haldia, the Committee recommends that Government should
extend adequate financial support to these major Ports for meeting their dredging and other
requirements. (Para: 30)
The Committee also recommends that the five projects cited above, for which no allocations
have been made in 2015-16, should also be considered for providing sufficient funds at RE stage
so that these vital projects remain operational. The Ministry should pursue this issue vigorously
with the Ministry of Finance. (Para: 31)
The Committee appreciates the new scheme aimed at controlling oil pollution in the Major
Ports and oil handling non-major ports under State Governments. The Committee feels that
pollution control should be given due attention in view of the increasing trend of pollution
through various means. The Committee, therefore, recommends that for those Major Ports who

35
are not in a financial position to afford the 50% cost of the pollution control equipments,
provisions for an additional support may be made in the scheme. (Para: 33)
Capacity Addition
The Committee notes the various ongoing projects for capacity addition in the Major Ports
and recommends that the completion of projects need to be expedited. (Para: 36)
The Committee notes the initiatives taken for Por t capacity addition till now. The Committee
also notes that so far during the mid of 12th Plan period, only 165.17 Million Tonne Per Annum
is the capacity added to Major Ports. The Committee also observes the 12th Plan target fixed for
achieving the port capacity of the Major Ports by 2016-17 as 943.06 million tonnes with the
corresponding Port capacity as 1229.24 million tonnes. The Committee feels that for achieving
the target of 1229.24 MTPA, the Major Ports would have to work very hard. The Committee
recommends that the Major Ports' capacity addition needs to be done at faster pace and that
enough funds for the purpose should be allocated by the Ministry. (Para: 40)
Sagarmala Project
The Committee welcomes the new project named Sagarmala for integrated development of
Indian Ports and Shipping Sectors. The Committee hopes that this project will be a key component
in the participation of the Indian Port and Shipping industry in the 'Make in India' Campaign
of the Prime Minister. (Para: 42)
The Committee desires to know the developments made in the establishment of two new
Major Ports in West Bengal and erstwhile Andhra Pradesh. The Committee also desires to know
the VGF the Central Government sanctioned in each of these ports. (Para: 43)
Cargo Traffic at Indian Ports
The Committee notes the performance of the Ports in terms of handling cargo traffic
during the last two years. The Committee is concerned to note that many of the Major Ports are
losing its business due to the presence of other Minor Ports in its close vicinity. The Committee
recommends that Major Ports should be equipped with modern facilities for handling of cargo so
that they can compete with the Non-Major Ports in the aspect of attracting more cargo.
(Para: 48)
The Committee understands that all the Major Ports have enough land available with them
and hence, providing proper storage facilities should not be a problem for them. Therefore, the
Committee recommends that all the Major Por ts should make sure that air-conditioned storage
facilities are available, so that there will not be any loss of cargo in the Ports. The Ministry
should make the necessary allocation at the RE stage and the Committee may be apprised of
the progress made in this regard. (Para: 49)
Port Efficiency
The Committee takes note of the improvement in Turnaround Time registered during
2013-14 in majority of the Major Ports and the increase in average output per ship per berth day.
The Committee hopes that the Major Ports would sustain this momentum in 2015-16 also.
(Para: 51)
The Committee desires that the Ministry should give adequate attention to enable efficient
electronic data interchange. The Committee hopes that such a system would save time and
resources. (Para: 53)

36
Tariff Authority on Major Ports (TAMP)
The Committee observes the flexibility given to the Major Ports to change tariff based on
market condition, as per the new Tariff Policy. The Committee hopes that this initiative would
enable not only more functional autonomy but also permit a level playing field to compete with
the minor ports who are not under the TAMP. The Committee finds that its repeated
recommendations in this regard have been considered by the Ministry while reviewing the TAMP
norms.
The Committee recommends that the revision of TAMP should be made effective at the
earliest. The Committee reiterates that the Ministry should consider constituting a port promotion
council to take initiative on the developmental activities as well as the proper marketing of the
services available with the Port and setting up a tribunal to hear complaints against port tariffs.
(Para: 57)
Road Connectivity to Ports
The Committee desires that Chennai-Ennore Port Road Connectivity Project should be
completed at the earliest for an increased traffic growth of the Chennai and Ennore Ports. The
Committee hopes that the meetings between the Chennai Port and the State Government prove
to be fruitful in addressing the issue of shifting of project affected persons. (Para: 59)
The Committee notes that the 4-Lane elevated road from Chennai Port to Maduravoyal
is a long delayed project. As a result thereof, the roads connecting to the Port premises get
choked with containers and trucks. This is not only causing inconvenience to the general public,
but also revenue loss to the Port. The Committee recommends that the issues with the State
Government of Tamil Nadu should be settled without further delay, so that the road project is
completed at the earliest. (Para: 60)
The Committee urges the Ministry to ensure that the progress of the other projects cited
above, proceed on a steady pace and are completed within the stipulated time. (Para: 61)
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should take proactive steps to
engage with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways so that the bottlenecks in the road
connectivity projects to the Ports are settled and the works progress steadily. (Para: 62)
Dredging Corporation of India (DCI)
The Committee notes that less allocations made for Cochin Port, Haldia Dock and
Visakhapatnam Port will adversely affect the revenue earnings of the DCI also, as most of the
dredging works at these Major Ports are carried out by the DCI. The Committee is of the
considered view that the Ministry should address this issue. (Para: 69)
The Committee finds that the DCI has managed to reduce its operational losses during the
last two years and finally register profit. The increased efficiency of the DCI is appreciable and
the Committee hopes that this momentum would be maintained in future also. (Para: 70)
The Committee understands that DCI had been in a financial crunch due to its outstanding
dues from various Ports and other agencies which now amounts to Rs 694.14 crores. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry of Shipping should take initiatives to release the outstanding dues
for paymentto DCI by the Organizations and Ports under them, within the least possible time.
The Committee emphasizes that the Ministry should play an active role in this regard.
(Para: 71)

37
The Committee desires that since the DCI is now in a financially better position, they may
consider increasing their dredging capacity in view of the requirement of the Major Ports in the
country. (Para: 72)
The Committee fails to understand why the DCI is in bad shape particularly where there
is tremendous dredging work to be done in our Ports in India. Its manpower and infrastructure
may be utilized by inspiring its professional competence and giving it modern machines so that
it can do dredging works in a big way. (Para:73)
Shipping Sector
The Committee notes that one of the reasons given for under-utilization by the light
houses is monsoon. The Committee feels that since this is a perennial phenomenon, the Ministry
should have anticipated it and taken steps to obviate delays caused due to it. (Para: 76)
The Committee takes serious note of the delay in submission of the SFC proposal by IMU.
The Committee finds that only about 40% of the funds allocated under the IWT were utilized.
The Committee stresses upon the need to maintain better fiscal discipline. The Committee is of
the view that this reveals lack of proper planning and the Committee strongly recommends that
the Ministry should chalk out strategies which are viable and ensure periodical monitoring of the
progress made in this regard. (Para: 77)
The Committee hopes that the e-Pariksha system will facilitate the candidates. The
Committee welcomes the pollution control measures taken by the Ministry through the ballast
water management program, in conformity with the International Convention. The Committee
hopes that construction work of the office of the DG Shipping will be completed in a time bound
manner. (Para: 80)
The Committee would like to know the details of the Scheme and the Ports covered under
this Scheme in 2015-16. (Para: 82)
The Committee notes the allocation made and suggests that the Ministry should take
adequate steps to utilize the allocation. (Para: 84)
Expansion of Indian Tonnage
The Committee notes that Indian vessels are older than the international average age of
16.7 years. The Committee feels that this could be one of the reasons for the sharp decline in
Indian overseas sea borne trade, over the years. (Para: 87)
The Committee desires that the Ministry should address this issue on priority basis and
furnish a detailed note in this regard. (Para: 88)
The Committee notes the various measures the Government has taken to boost the Indian
tonnage. The Committee is of the opinion that by allowing shipping enterprises based in India
to acquire ships abroad and flag them in the country of their convenience, the country is losing
out on tax money. The Committee feels that the better way out is that the Government should
revisit its existing wrong policies and norms that prevent Indian Ship owners from registering
their vessels in India and make necessary changes therein. The Committee further recommends
that abatement of service tax on the tonnage of goods should be uniform in all sectors of
transport viz., rail, road and waterways. (Para: 91)
Shipping Corporation of India Ltd.
The Committee takes note of the reasons given for loss of SCI during the last two fiscals.
It is encouraging to see that the extent of loss has declined. The Committee takes the depressed

38
market as the reason for loss of SCI with a pinch of salt. It endorses the decision to hold the
purchase orders of vessels by the SCI until it made up its previous losses. The Committee hopes
that a cautious approach needs to be adopted by SCI in future for avoiding the losses that have
been suffered in the recent years. An aggressive approach coupled with positive initiatives, would
enable SCI to improve its performance. (Para: 95)
Ship Building Industry
The Ministry has also stated that ship building industry in India has to borrow working
capital on long term basis. In India, the interest rates are high ranging from 13 to 16% for long
term and short term loans while in many foreign countries like China and Korea it is as low as
2.75%. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that subsidy on interest payment should be
given by the Government to ship building industry in order to attract more investment in this
sector. The Committee also recommends that domestic buyers should be encouraged to buy ship
from Indian ship manufacturers. (Para: 97)
The Committee understands that ship building industry depends on large numbers of
ancillary industries like steel, electronics heavy engineering equipment etc. The Committee
desires that such ancillary industries also should be encouraged who supply indigenous equipments
for ship building. (Para: 98)
The Committee also notes that availability of skilled labour and labour productivity need
to be improved in the ship building sector. The Committee emphasizes the need for ensuring that
our educational system and skill development facilities should be modernized to ensure quality
labour force in the ship building sector. The Committee also recommends for R&D facility for
modern ship designs in the country. (Para:99)
Cochin Shipyard Ltd.
The Committee takes note of the performance of the Cochin Shipyard during the last two
years as also the activities proposed during 2015-16. (Para: 104)
In India, we have huge scientific and technological human resources. However, these
resources are not fine tuned to support specific industrial and technological activities. The
Committee observes that there is a need to fine tune our human resources to support the ship
building industry of our country. (Para: 105)
The Committee observes that eventhough Cochin Shipyard was the only shipyard with the
Ministry, it is not equipped with modern equipments and trained manpower to be able to reach
the global standards. They also are starved of funds as it is evident that Cochin Shipyard has
got no money allocated for its activities proposed for 2015-16. In such a situation they do not
have any major work mainly because they cannot afford to do that. The Committee feels that
this trend needs to be changed in the current situation. The Committee stresses upon the urgent
need for taking up all out modernization and capacity building of this Shipyard to give a boost
to the ship building industry in the country. (Para: 106)
The Committee recommends that the Shipbuilding Sector should be linked with the 'Make
In India' programme and that our shipyards should be modernized so that they can compete with
the best of foreign shipyards. The Ministry should also ensure that skilled manpower is made
available to cope with the situation. (Para: 107)

39
Hooghly Dock and Port Engineers Limited
The Committee desires that the Ministry should take up a detailed SWOT (Strength,
Weakness, Opportunities, Threats) analysis of this Organization and take remedial steps to
revive HDPEL. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should explore the possibility of
linking HDPEL with the Make in India programme. (Para: 109)
Directorate General Lighthouse and Lightships
The Committee notes the activities completed by the DG Lighthouses and Lightships
during 2014-15 and the plans proposed for 2015-16. The Committee recommends for time bound
completion of the projects so that the funds do not lapse at later stage. (Para: 113)
The Committee notes that every lighthouse of olden era has many stories to tell; the
stories of adventurism, conquer, miracles, heroism and so on. The Committee recommends that
the Government should explore the historical values of the lighthouses and make use of them
to promote tourism and pride among the people. (Para: 115)
The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken by the Ministry. The Committee reiterates
its previous recommendation that lighthouses must be made tourist spots and thereby, they could
generate extra income for its operations. (Para: 116)
INLAND WATERWAY AUTHORITY OF INDIA (IWAI)
The Committee notes that reductions in allocation for IWT at RE stage were done despite
the request not to do so. It did af fect its on-going works adversely . The Committee recommends
that the Ministry of Finance should take this Sector seriously and accordingly ensure that such
abrupt cut is not repeated. This Sector needs massive funds for exploring its potential. Money
should be mobilized from all possible sources. (Para: 119)
The Committee notes that there is no allocation made for NW-2 during 2015-16. In the
case of NW-3 also, the allocation is inadequate. The Committee recommends that adequate funds
for NW-2 and NW-3 in the current financial year should be provided at the RE stage.
(Para: 122)
The Committee notes that Inland Waterways which had been the mainstay of transportation
in India, remain highly neglected in the recent times. If developed properly, the potential and
benefits of inland waterways are immense which if exploited can give unprecedented boost to the
transport sector and our economy. The Committee also notes that only around 20% of the total
12th Plan outlay has been utilized so far in the IWT sector which is highly disappointing for
whatever reasons. The Committee recommends that more focus should be given to IWT sector
so that the funds allocated are spent and all the proposed projects are completed by the end of
the 12th Plan period. (Para: 123)
Physical Infrastructure Projects of NWs
The Committee notes the various targets set by the Ministry and the phases of construction
going on at various Waterways. The Committee is surprised to see that work at NW-4 and NW-
5 is yet to commence even after several years. The Committee hopes that this work would start,
as per the schedules stated by the Ministry. The Committee notes that the development and
dredging work of the Trivandrum-Kollam stretch of the NW-2 (Parwati Puthanaar) is pending for
a long time and recommends that the work should be started at the earliest. The Committee
desires that adequate funds should be allocated for the purpose. (Para: 125)

40
The Committee also recommends that dredgers and other machineries available with the
Dredging Corporation of India should be utilized for dredging works at the Waterways, wherever
possible. (Para: 126)
Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Ltd. (CIWTC)
The Committee notes the reply. (Para: 129)
INDIAN MARITIME UNIVERSITY
The Committee feels that in this case, had the concerned people been attentive and
proactive, its plan would entirely have been approved on time avoiding thereby non-utilization
of scarce funds with the Ministry. The Committee desires that the Standing Finance Committee
should get the approval process completed urgently. (Para: 133)
The Committee, during its deliberations, took strong exception to the mismanagement of
IMU. The Committee also learnt from various sources about alleged irregularities in the IMU.
The Committee feels that there should be greater transparency and accountability in the matters
of IMU. The Committee desires that the Ministry should ensure periodic and strict monitoring
of IMU. (Para: 135)
The Committee recommends that research oriented activities should be given priority in
IMU. The Committee further emphasizes that the syllabus and curriculum of IMU should be
prepared as per the current day market requirement and that the University should ensure that
job avenues are made available to the students. The Committee also desires that the Ministry
may furnish the data on the number of students of IMU who got their placements by way of
campus selection, till date. (Para: 136)
Taxation in the Shipping Sector
The Committee recommends that the Government may consider granting NRI status to
seafarers serving in Indian flagships. The Committee also recommends for tax incentives for
income from sale for qualifying vessels and other tax incentives requested by the Ministry of
Shipping during the pre- budget memorandum. The Committee further recommends that Ministry
of Finance may examine the feasibility of the various indirect tax incentives requested by the
Ministry of Shipping that may give a boost to the Shipping industry in the country. The Ministry
should take up the issues with the concerned Ministries/Departments and submit a note to this
Committee along with the responses from them. (Para: 138)
Legislative Measures
The Committee, in its 197th Report, had made recommendations on the Merchant Shipping
(First Amendment) Bill, 2014 on the anti-fouling systems for control of chemical pollution in the
seas. The Committee understands that the legislation has been implemented w.e.f 1st April, 2015
and hopes that this legislation would help in controlling the use of harmful anti-fouling systems
on ships. (Para: 140)
The Committee, in its 202nd Report, had made recommendations on the implementation
of Maritime Labour Convention 2006 for the benefits of the Indian seafarers. The Committee
notes that seafarers are facing various problems, cheating and other atrocities even from ship
owners and life threat from pirates etc. throughout their career. Even though there are provisions
for their protection under the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, they have not proved to be effective

41
in addressing their grievances. The Committee, therefore, recommends for an early
implementation of the Maritime Labour Convention 2006. (Para: 142)
Vacancies
The Committee notes that due to non- availability of sufficient personnel in the customs
department, the ports are not able to make swift cargo movement or work round the clock.
Customs is income earning venture of the exchequer. Therefore, the Government should augment
its income earning capacity by deputing sufficient number of officials to man the customs
activities at the ports. Recruitment of customs personnel will help the already struggling ports
to streamline its operations. The Committee recommends that this matter should be considered
seriously and adequate steps for recruiting enough staff members should be taken immediately.
(Para: 144)
The Committee takes strong exception to the proposal of Ministry of Finance for installing
container scanners in every port in adequate numbers. But this work is not being done with
required scale and pace. As a result we are still running the risk of radio active and other
hazardous material including lethal weapons into the country. The Committee would like to have
a status note on installation work of scanner at our Ports reflecting the requirements and
actually installed/ sanctioned, Port-wise. (Para: 145)
The Committee notes the vacancies existing in the Ministry and recommends that the
Ministry should take steps to ensure that the vacancies are filled up without delay.  (Para: 147)
Komagata Maru Memorial
The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the Ministry of Shipping. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry of Culture should provide the required grant for construction of
the memorial. The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism has a scheme to fund the
Central Government agencies for maintaining monuments. The Committee recommends that
the Ministry of Tourism may also be approached for appropriate funding for construction of the
monument as it can attract a large number of tourists. (Para: 154)
Other Issues
The Committee understands that low lying structures along the NW-3 cause hindrance to
the development of the Waterways in Kerala and at many stretches, the issue is a major one.
The Committee hopes that the new Bill will be able to address such issues and that the pace of
development of National Waterways will increase after the implementation of the Act.
(Para: 156)
The Committee notes that insufficiency of rakes is a perennial problem and despite being
pointed out year after year, resolution of this issue is still out of sight. The Committee feels that
this is happening because of the inefficient planning by the agencies concerned. The Committee
recommends that a solution to the problem may be found out urgently keeping in view the long
term requirements. The Committee hopes that the Infrastructure Committee would be able to
address the infrastructure related issues in consultation with all the other agencies concerned.
(Para: 158)
The Committee urges the Ministry to look into the matter urgently and apprise the
Committee, the steps taken to alleviate the problem. (Para: 160)

42
General Observations and Recommendations
During the discussion on Demands for Grants, the Members of the Committee highlighted
the need for better utilization of the vacant land available with the Major Ports. The Committee
recommends that unutilized land with the Major Ports should be utilized appropriately in public
interest such as hospitals, schools etc. The Ministry should also ensure that encroachments from
its land are removed and that new encroachments are not allowed to happen. (Para: 161)
The Committee emphasizes the need for greater autonomy-financial and administrative-
to be given to Major Ports, so that they may be able to tackle the rough patches in the execution
of projects without delay and execute their projects timely. (Para: 162)
The Committee recommends that Vizhinjam Port in Kerala which has natural draft of 16ft,
should be developed properly with the aid of the Central Government. The Committee also
recommends that the present cabotage regulations which are preventing the Port from getting
a suitable bidder should be revisited and corrective measures should be taken promptly.
(Para: 163)
The Committee observes that oil pilferage is a huge environmental issue and recommends
that the Government should take corrective measures to contain this menace. The Committee
desires that environmental pollution from asbestos due to ship breaking also needs to be addressed
effectively. (Para:164)
The Committee urges the Ministry that for skill development in the various trades of the
Shipping Sector, the Ministry, Shipping Corporation of India, Ports etc. should sponsor such
courses in the IITs and other reputed Institutes of the country. (Para:165)
The Committee recommends that small barges up to 500 tone capacity should be given
adequate subsidy to improve transportation through inland waterways. (Para:166)
The Committee also observes that due to scarcity of large sized scanners, customs/ security
checking of the large sized cargo get delayed in the Ports. The Committee recommends that
necessary remedial steps should be taken in this matter. (Para: 167)

2. The Chair welcomed the Secretary and other officials of the Ministry of Shipping and its subordinate
organizations. The Chair asked the Secretary to make a presentation on the Budget allocations, expenditure,
achievements, non-utilization of funds, the adequacy of budgetary provisions made to each head etc. The
Committee wanted to know about the areas where the Ministry failed to fully utilize the funds, the details
of fund allocations to the port sector, shipping sector, capacity addition of ports, issues related to
Shipping Corporation of India, Dredging Corporation of India, Indian Maritime University, development
of Inland Waterways, issues related to Kolkata Port and Haldia, Cochin Port, Mumbai Port, road projects
in the Ports, use of Port land for the benefit of general public, the schemes for infrastructure development
in enhancing port capacity, providing boost to the ship building industry etc.
3. The Secretary gave an overview on the budget allocation made for the Ministry and the achievements
made during the previous years. He briefed the Committee about the reasons for under utilization of
funds, the achievements made during the 12th Plan, issues related to the major ports and other organizations
under the Ministry, their future plans etc. The Secretary gave a comparative table on the expenditure

48
made under various sectors during the period from 5th Plan to 11th Plan. He explained to the Committee
that Railways got the highest allocation of 51.53%, followed by Road Transport with 32.54% allocation.
However, Civil Aviation got 9.46% and the least allocation was given to Water Transport which was mere
6.47%.
4. The Secretary apprised the Committee that about 101 navigable main rivers are available in the
country for navigation. However, indiscriminate construction of cross-structures in them are causing a
major hindrance to navigation. Therefore, Cabinet has approved introduction of a Bill in Parliament to
bring some regulation of such structures across the rivers in the country. He stated that availability of
sufficient rakes is a major problem faced by the Ports, especially the Major Ports located in the eastern
coast. To address this issue, an Infrastructure Committee has been constituted under the Chairmanship
of the Minister for Shipping and the Committee holds periodic meetings to review the status.
5. The Members of the Committee highlighted the need for scanners of large sized containers at
Major ports, controlling pollution caused by oil spilling, asbestos during ship breaking etc.
6. Members of the Committee also raised various queries. The Secretary replied to the points raised.
The Chair directed that written replies to the points not answered, may be sent within a week.
7. A verbatim record of the proceedings was kept.

REPORT
Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency for the formulation of national policies and
programmes for the development and promotion of tourism in the country. In the process, the
Ministry consults and collaborates with other stakeholders in the sector including various Central
Ministries/agencies, the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations and the representatives of
the private sector.
2. The administrative head of the Ministry is the Secretary (Tourism). The Secretary also acts as
the Director General (DG) Tourism. Directorate General of Tourism has a field formation of 20
offices within the country and 14 offices abroad and one sub-ordinate office/project i.e. Indian
Institute of Skiing and Mountaineering (IISM)/Gulmarg Winter Sports Project. The overseas offices
are primarily responsible for tourism promotion and marketing in their respective areas and the field
offices in India are responsible for providing information service to tourists and to monitor the
progress of field projects.
3. Tourism is promoted within India primarily by the Ministry of Tourism with the help of 5
Regional Offices and 15 Sub-Offices under them, with the involvement of the State Governments and
with the help of modern and conventional tools of promotion. India Tourism Development
Corporation (ITDC) is the only public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Tourism.
4. The Ministry also has the autonomous institutions viz., Indian Institutes of Tourism and Travel
Management (IITTM); National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology (NCHMCT);
and the 21 Institutes of Hotel Management (IHMs).
5. The major Programmes/Schemes of the Ministry of Tourism are:–
(i) Product/Infrastructure Development for Destinations and Circuits;
(ii) Overseas Promotion and Publicity including Market Development Assistance;
(iii) Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/NIWS (National Institute of Water Sports);
(iv) Domestic Promotion and Publicity including Hospitality;
(v) Capacity Building for Service Providers;
(vi) Incentives to Accommodation Infrastructure;
(vii) Computerization and Information Technology;
(viii) Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Projects;
(ix) Externally Aided Projects;
(x) Market Research including 20 Years Perspective Plans;
(xi) Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development;
(xii) Integrated Development of Theme-Based Tourist Circuits - SW ADESH DARSHAN; and
(xiii) National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation And Spiritual Augmentation Drive
(PRASAD).

Secretary, Ministry of Tourism along with other senior officials explained to the Committee various
aspects of the Demands for Grants. The Committee also sought information through a questionnaire
on various issues related to the Ministry.

9. The Committee notes that even though Planning Commission had made a very
ambitious plan for tourism promotion in the country during the 12th plan Period by making
an outlay of Rs. 15190 crore, the sanctions made during the first three years of the Twelfth
Plan period was Rs. 2930.00 crore only, which is just 19.28% of the total outlay. If the actual
spending is taken into consideration, it stands at Rs. 2566.48 crore which is 16.89% of the
12th Plan outlay. The Committee finds that expenditure and allocation have not been upto the
mark. It is a matter of concern as the targets also could not have been achieved due to less
spending. The Committee, therefore, is constrained to observe that such a pattern does not
augur well for Tourism, as it has highest potential for employment as well as revenue
generation for our economy.
10. The Government does not make adequate allocation for this Sector. The Committee is
afraid that if such a trend continues, the country may not be able to sustain the current
tourist inflow, not to speak of increasing it upto the desired level. It, therefore, may result
in the decline of not only the tourism industry as a whole but also so many other sectors
associated with it.

Clean India Campaign
51. The Ministry has taken the initiative to launch Campaign Clean India to create awareness about
cleanliness and its impact on promotion of tourism. This campaign is sustained through adoption of
monuments and tourist destinations by corporate sector/PSUs as a part of their corporate social
responsibility (CSR). It is a voluntary scheme and there is no budget allocation by the Government
for this campaign. The Ministry of Tourism acts only as a facilitator.
52. The following agencies have adopted certain monuments as per the details
(i) India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) has adopted Qutab Minar, New Delhi as
a Pilot Project under Campaign Clean India. The various works undertaken by ITDC
include repair of toilets, proper signages in and around Qutab Minar, garbage bins, repair/

12
replacement of light covers and painting of railings and deployment of staff for regular
maintenance.
(ii) ONGC has adopted six monuments namely viz.,  Taj Mahal at Agra, Ellora Caves,
Elephanta Caves, Red Fort in Delhi, Golkonda Fort and Mahabalipuram. ONGC has taken
a holistic approach for overall up-gradation, beautification including cleanliness and
maintenance of the monuments. The ONGC has approved cost estimates of Rs.20.75
crores for Taj Mahal Project. MOU has been signed between ASI, ONGC and Ministry
of Tourism on 25.9.2014 at the function organized at Red Fort, New Delhi for
undertaking various works at Taj Mahal. The implementation of above works would be
undertaken by ASI.
(iii) Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL) have expressed their willingness to adopt Gateway
of India in Mumbai and Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar. The meetings have been held with
District Magistrate, Haridwar and with Municipal Commissioner, BMC, Mumbai to
discuss adoption of these places. Site inspections have been carried out both at Gateway
of India and Har Ki Pauri. Further action will be initiated after hearing from BMC
Mumbai and DM, Haridwar.
(iv) The National Building Construction Corporation Ltd. (NBCC) has expressed their
willingness to adopt Fatehpur Sikri in Agra under Campaign Clean India. The proposal
has been forwarded to DG , ASI for further action.
(v) For regular upkeep and maintenance, 12 ghats at Varanasi were offered for adoption to
the corporate sector such as hoteliers, tour operators and Sulabh International. Sulabh
International has opted to look after cleanliness of six ghats viz. Ahilya Ghat, Darbhanga
Ghat, Ranamahal Ghat, Digipatiya Ghat, Chausathi Ghat and Munshi Ghat. Out of these
six ghats, Sulabh International has signed MOU with Nagar Nigam, Varanasi in respect
of Darbhanga ghat, Ahilya ghat and Munshi ghat for cleanliness and maintenance.
53. The Committee appreciates the initiatives made by the Ministry. The Committee
acknowledges that ITDC has been the pioneer in this field. The Committee notes that
compared to previous years, more PSUs have come forward as part of their Corporate Social
Responsibility to adopt monuments and important tourism sites for their upkeep and
maintenance.

of tourist spots/monuments of the country. The Committee recommends that the Government

88. The Government of India launched the Tourist Visa on Arrival (TVoA) enabled with Electronic
Travel Authorisation (ETA) Scheme on 27.11.2014. This facility is available to foreigners whose sole
objective of visiting India is recreation, sight- seeing, short duration medical treatment, casual
business visit, casual visit to meet friends or relatives etc. and not valid for any other purpose/
activities. This will allow entry into India within 30 days from the date of approval of ETA and will
be valid for 30 days stay in India from the date of arrival in India. The TV oA enabled with ETA cannot
be availed more than twice in a calendar year.
89. The Ministry has further stated that the TV oA enabled with ETA would enable the prospective
visitor to apply for an Indian Visa from his/her home country online without visiting the Indian
Mission and also pay the visa fee online. Once approved, the applicant will receive an email
authorizing him/her to travel to India and he/she can travel with a print out of this authorization. On
arrival, the visitor has to present the authorization to the immigration authorities who would then
stamp the entry into the country.
90. With effect from 15.1.2015, Guyana was added to this list thereby making it a total of 44
countries whose citizens are eligible for this facility. During the last three months, 87610 TV oAs have
been issued.

to 150 countries in stages, the Ministry of Tourism has submitted a list of 106 additional countries

Tourism has taken following steps:

28
(i) The Ministry of Tourism, on a pilot basis, has set up the 'Incredible India Help Line' to
address and guide the tourists during any emergencies which may include medical,
crime, natural calamities or on being stranded. This service will be available as toll free
on telephone 1800111363 or on a short code 1363 and is accessible 24x7 and 365 to
provide an authentic information to tourists and also guide them during emergencies once
they are in India.
(ii) Grant of Central Financial Assistance to Government of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and
Andhra Pradesh for setting up of Tourist Facilitation and Security Organization (TFSO)
on a pilot basis.
(iii) Adoption of code of conduct for Safe and Honorable Tourism, which contains a set of
guidelines to encourage tourism activities to be undertaken with respect to basic rights
like dignity, safety and freedom from exploitation of both tourists and local residents, in
particular women and children.
(iv) All the Chief Ministers of the State Governments and Administrators of Union Territory
Administrations have been asked to take immediate effective steps for ensuring a
conducive and friendly environment for all tourists and also request them to publicize the
steps being taken/proposed to be taken to increase the sense of security amongst the
present/prospective visitors and also to counter the negative publicity.
(v) In the wake of some unfortunate incidents involving foreign tourists, Ministry of
Tourism has also posted an advisory on its website www.incredibleindia.org.
145. Ministry of Tourism has advised all the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations to
deploy Tourist Police in the States/Union Territories.
146. The State Governments/Union Territory Administrations of Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Goa,
Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha,
Punjab, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh have deployed Tourist Police, in one form or the other.
147. The Committee notes the various measures taken for ensuring safety and security of
the tourists in the country. The Committee recommends that:
(i) Along with the help line numbers published, the tourists should have a direct
access to police and such enforcement authorities.
(ii) All the major railway stations, bus stations also must carry tourist help desks
24X7.
(iii) All major tourist centres should display the guidelines and helpline numbers for
the use of tourists.
(iv) It should be made compulsory that on a twice a week basis, each foreign tourist
should report to a nearest information centre about their next place of visit and
the details of accommodation etc.
ITDC
148. India Tourism Development Corporation came into existence in the year 1966 after merging
three Corporations which had been existing under the Government for a few years and later on,
Ashoka Hotel and Janpath Hotel got merged and then, it started functioning.

29
149. The Secretary, Ministry of Tourism informed the Committee that in the year 2002-03, there
was heavy disinvestment of a large number of hotels, after which that, the phase of consolidation
started. Thereafter, ITDC remained in profit for almost all the years except the year 2011-12. In the
year 2012-13, the turnover of ITDC was Rs. 440 crores which increased to about Rs. 470 crores
in the year 2013-14, and the profit after tax trebled. The Secretary stated that ITDC is expected to
register profits in 2014-15.
150. Right now, ITDC has eight hotels and six joint venture hotels. Apart from that, it has two
managed units, one at Bharatpur and other at Kosi, on the way to Agra. ITDC has duty-free shop
also at one airport. ITDC has started getting sea ports as duty free shops because it is found very
profitable and new openings are also available.
151. The Committee notes the progress made by ITDC in the recent years, but feels that
that standard and upkeep of accommodation and food in ITDC hotels leave much to be
desired.  Budget hotels are giving serious challenge to its existing hotels. The Committee
recommends that ITDC may explore the possibilities of undertaking tour packages under the
LTC package, as done by the IRCTC.
Transparency Initiatives
152. A web-based Public Delivery System for recognition of the Travel Trade Service Providers has
been set up in the Ministry. The new procedure accepts applications online from service providers
and thereby makes the process paperless also. All the applications are to be submitted online and will
be examined, processed and approved/rejected within 45 days from the receipt of completed
applications.
153. The Committee appreciates the initiative of the Ministry and hopes that this would
ensure greater transparency and quick processing of applications.
154. The Committee appreciates the following initiatives taken by the Ministry, as stated in
its Annual Report (2014-15):-
Medical Tourism
(i) The Ministry revised guidelines for the promotion of Medical Tourism as a Niche
Tourism Product on 21st August, 2014.
(ii) India excels among the several Asian destinations like Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand
that are offering Medical care facilities and promoting Medical Tourism as there is no
waiting time for availing the medical services.
(iii) 'Medical Visa' has been introduced, which can be given for specific purpose to foreign
tourists coming to India for medical treatment.
(iv) During the year 2014-15 (till December, 2014), the Ministry under Market Development
Assistance (MDA) scheme provided a financial assistance of Rs. 20, 25, 000/- to the
Medical Tourism Service Providers.
Wellness Tourism
(i) During the year 2014-15 (till December, 2014), the Ministry under MDA scheme
provided a financial assistance of Rs. 64, 69, 535/- to the Service Providers.

30
(ii) Y oga/Ayurveda/Wellness has been promoted in the past years in the print, electronic,
internet and outdoor medium under this Ministry's "Incredible India Campaign".
Golf Tourism
155. The Ministry constituted the India Golf Tourism Committee (IGTC), which is the nodal body
for golf tourism in the country. The IGTC approved 11 golf events during the year 2014-15 (till
December, 2014) and released an amount of Rs 2,30,46,706/-.
Polo Tourism
156. During the year 2014-15, the Ministry released an amount of Rs 5.00 lakh as Central Financial
Assistance to the Manipur Horse Riding and Polo Association, Imphal, Manipur for organizing 6th
Manipur Polo International.
Film Tourism
157. During the year 2014-15, the Ministry of Tourism has reimbursed an amount of Rs. 79,76,936/-
to the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) on account of promotion of Film Tourism. The
Ministry has also instituted a National Tourism Award for the "Most Film Promotion Friendly State/UT".
Caravan Tourism
158. The Ministry recently introduced Caravan Policy. Caravans are unique tourism products that
promote family oriented tours in circuits/destinations not having adequate hotel accommodation.
159. There are so many ideasconcepts in this vast and multifaceted country and a lot has to
do as mentioned above. The Committee hopes that the efforts being made by the Ministry
would prove to be fruitful in the coming years.
OTHER OBSERV ATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
160. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism may develop a comprehensive
Mobile Application for the use of the tourists, and all the tourism service providers which will
enable them to access all the authenticated data about tourism in India.
161. The Committee was informed that the Komagata Maru Memorial in Kolkata Port
remains neglected and has poor maintenance. In view of its great historical importance, the
Committee recommends that Komagata Maru Memorial in Kolkata Port may be developed
suitably to attract tourists by pooling efforts and funds from Ministries of Shipping, Culture
and Tourism in order to respect the sacrifices made by our people.
162. The Committee notes that many of the tourists are availing services of roadside dhabas
and eateries, but they are functioning without much help and assistance from the Government
agencies. The Committee recommends that these need to be guided/helped in all possible
manner for making them tourist-friendly, cleaner  and hygienic, serving local cuisine in local
ambience. They should be incentivized to serve the tourists better.
163. The Committee noted that the Sindhu Darshan programme is running without much
assistance from the Government. The programme needs to be publicized and tourists may be
provided with better facilities there. The Committee recommends that financial support

31
should be extended to Sindhu Darshan Programme.
164. The Committee recommends that Gogamedi Festival in Rajasthan also may be promoted
under a suitable scheme by the Ministry of Tourism.
165. The Committee finds that no transparent formula for pricing of air tickets is available
in the country at present as the air fares being charged by the airlines operating in the
country are on the higher side, which is a deterrent for tourism development in the country.
The Committee notes that there is no rationality or even fixed parameters to be followed for
fixing the airfares. The Committee, therefore, emphasizes the need for fixing a cap on the
lower and maximum air fare to be charged during the peak and non-peak seasons with a view
to bring more transparency in fixation of affordable airfare for the passengers. The
Committee, therefore, desires the Ministry to take up this issue with the Ministry of Civil
Aviation to have a regulatory mechanism for fixing the airfare at affordable level.
166. To conclude, the Committee has noteed that its major scheme- the PIDDC is being
implemented by the States, who have to follow procedures etc. Had the Ministry of Tourism
been a little proactive, it may have made a lot of improvement in implementing these
projects/programmes. The Committee could not find much problem in respect of availability
of funds, but a proper monitoring and close co-ordination among States for executing the
projects would have done wonders. It would have avoided lapsing of funds in most of the
projects. The Committee hopes that with the devolution of funds to the States and non-
allocation to its Centrally Sponsored Scheme- PIDDC, the excuse of the Ministry of Tourism
that States go slow will no more be there. It is hoped that such schemes will be executed by
the States with greater efficiency and pr omptness now. This will also leave enough time to the
Union Ministry for implementing Central Sector Schemes-older as well as new ones. The
Committee would like to extend its best wishes to the Ministry. The Committee desired that
the Ministry of Tourism should improve its performance in the coming years.
167. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should desire strategic road maps for
each scheme/programme and monitor and evaluate them periodically. This would ensure that
bottlenecks are cleared up promptly.
