Shipping for carrying out their various projects pr oposed to undertake in the financial 
year 2017-18.  The Ministry of Finance may be appro ached for getting enhanced allocation 
at RE stage. 
(Para: 22) 
 The Committee recommends that in order to fast-tra ck the works related to 
sagarmala, coastal shipping, IWT and ALHW,additiona l budgetary allocation may be 
provided to Ministry of Shipping during 2017-18. 
(Para: 23) 
PORT SECTOR 
 The Committee notes that the allocation made to Po rt Sector is highly insufficient to 
meet the committed liability of the various ports during 2017-18.  In the case of VoCPT, the 
capital dredging work has already completed and the y should release the balance amount 
of Rs.120.06 crore for which the allocation made is  only Rs.15.00 crore.  In the case of 
Chennai Port, their coastal road protection work is  completed by 80% and the payment is 
in midway. They also need 33 crores for completing the work.  The Cochin Port has two 
projects to be carried out which need 52 crore, but  the allocation is only 10 crore.  The 
activities under Swachh Bharat Abhiyan got nil allo cation this time.  The Committee 
strongly recommends that the Ministry of Finance ma y take a review of the situation after 
the completion of first quarter of  Financial Year 2017-18 and additional  allocation may be 
made as per their requirement thereafter. 
27

 
 
(Para: 28) 
Port Efficiency and Productivity: 
 The Committee notes that the port capacity has bee n enhanced during 2016-17 and 
the total capacity among the Major Ports is 1049.45  MTPA at the end of the last plan year.  
There is a considerable increase of capacity during  the 12 
th  Plan period.  During the period 
a total of 352.92 MT has increased.  The Committee is optimistic that the port capacity will 
further increase in the next plan period to accommo date the growth in EXIM trade of 
India. 
(Para: 35) 
 However, the Committee with a little dismay, has n oticed that the cargo growth is 
not up to the mark as per  the  figures given in th e beginning of the 12 th  Plan period.  The 
Committee notes that the growth of cargo traffic by  Major Ports are not  commensurating  
with the port capacity additions. The Committee als o notes that nine ports registered 
positive growth while four ports have been in the red.  The Committee recommends that all 
efforts should be explored to keep the cargo growth  in all the ports throughout the year. 
The ports who have registered negative growth durin g 2016-17 should workout effective 
plans to reverse the situation. 
(Para: 36) 
 The Committee notes that the Major Ports in Easter n Peninsula are struggling to 
make profits and its viability is in question. The coastal shipping is also not being improved 
at optimal level according to the potential of the country. The Committee observes that the 
viability of the Major Ports in the Eastern Peninsu la can be improved by coastal shipping 
by providing the facility of Sethusamudram canal. 
(Para: 37) 
Dredging 
 The Committee is happy to note that except for one  or two  Major Ports, all the 
others have maintained 14M draft and they are going  further ahead to achieve 18M depth.  
The Committee is optimist that in the coming years these  ports could accommodate larger 
vessels in the berths and thereby increase their cargo throughput. 
(Para: 40) 
 The Committee notes that the capital dredging work  of the Mormugao Port has 
been stalled due to withdrawal of the Environmental  clearance given to the projects. The 
Committee desires to know the decision of the Goa S tate Pollution Control Board on the 
matter when it is available. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Shipping may 
pursue the matter with the concerned authorities. 
(Para: 41) 
 The Committee notes that since the Kolkata Port be ing a riverine port, it requires 
frequent maintenance dredging to keep the desired d epth of the draft. The Committee 
recommends that required budgetary sanctions may be  given to Kolkata Port to meet the 
requirements. 
(Para: 42) 
Connectivity to Major Ports 
 The Committee notes that 42 road connectivity proj ects have been undertaken to 
link all the major ports in the country. The Committee recommends that required financial 
sanction may be made for timely completion of these  projects. The Committee also 
recommends that more projects which are not yet rec eived environmental clearance may 
pursue the matter with the Ministry of Environment & Forest. 
(Para: 46) 
28

 
 
SAGARMALA 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry of Shipping has ambitious future plans for 
carrying out port development work under Sagarmala Project.  The Committee also notes 
that Sagarmala Development Company Ltd. has been in corporated with an initial 
authorized capital of Rs.1000 crore for monitoring the projects.  The Committee desires to 
know the source of funds with the Ministry to achieve this ambitious target.  
(Para: 52) 
 The Committee also note that there are 199 focus p rojects targeted to be completed 
under Sagarmala in the next three financial years w ith an actual cost of Rs.333,534 crore.  
The Committee desires to know the details of financ ial plans with the Ministry of Shipping 
to generate that much resource within three years to meet the required fund for completion 
of the projects. The Committee recommends that fina ncial grants may be provided to 
projects under Sagarmala as per the requirement.  
(Para: 53) 
 The Committee feels that if the  projects under Sa garmala are completed as planned 
by the Ministry, it will not only boost the economi c activities  but also create employment 
opportunities in the country to the greatest extent.   
(Para: 54) 
SHIPPING SECTOR 
 The Committee notes that during 2016-17 out of the  GBS allocation of Rs.45.34 
crore at RE 2016-17 the Ministry of Shipping has sp ent Rs.42.05 crore so far.  Since two 
more months are there in  the financial year, the C ommittee hopes that they would be able 
to spend the entire allocation. 
(Para: 57) 
 The Committee notes from Annexure-I, the Ship Buil ding Sector has sought Rs.527 
core allocation during 2017-18 however, the actual allocation received is just Rs.12.00 
crore.  The Committee feels that this is highly ins ufficient.  The Committee recommends 
that sufficient funds may be allocated to Ship Building Sector. 
(Para: 58) 
 The Committee notes the various initiatives taken by the Ministry of Shipping has 
taken to improve the Shipping and Ship building Sector of the country. 
(Para: 60) 
DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF LIGHTHOUSES & LIGHT SHIPS 
 The Committee notes that the DGLL has undertaken v arious projects to establish 
six new light houses and 3 new lighted beacones at various parts of the country.  The 
Committee also notes the projects to be undertaken during 2017-18.  The Committee 
recommends that all these projects may be completed within the stipulated time frame. 
(Para: 65) 
 The Committee also notes the achievements for maki ng all the Lighthouses during 
solarised for the first time and also identifying for development of 8 lighthouses for tourism 
purposes through PPP mode. 
(Para: 66) 
 
 
 
COCHIN SHIPYARD LIMITED 
29

 
 
 The Committee is happy to note that the Cochin Shi pyard has been strong in 
financial performance during the current financial year. The Committee hopes that the 
targets will be attained at the end of the Financial Year. 
(Para: 72) 
 The Committee notes that the Indian ship yards are  less sophisticated and lacking 
world class standards of equipment and manpower.  S imilarly low cost loans are not easily 
available for expansion of the shipyard.  The Commi ttee recommends the following to 
support the ship building industry in the country: 
(i) The Government of India should take necessary steps  to upgrade the current 
technology used by the shipyards with the modern te chnology available  in 
worldwide; 
(ii) Periodic refreshment training of the existing employees may be conducted on 
regular basis to familiarize with the latest technology; 
(iii) Low cost loans may be raised from the overseas markets; and 
(iv) Tax incentives to the yards as well as subsidies to  the buyers may be 
expanded to attract more buyers from Indian market. 
(Para: 73) 
 The Committee has noted the assurances given by th e Secretary, Shipping and 
recommends that the Cochin shipyard should not be p rivatized or disinvested as it is 
functioning well under the Government of India control. 
(Para: 75) 
SHIPPING CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED 
 The Committee notes the financial performance of S CI during the last 3 years. The 
Committee further notes that the SCI has now recove red from its losses and continuously 
making profit for the last 3 years. The Committee d esired to know the reasons why the 
income has shown declining trend in the first half of the Financial Year 2016-17.  
(Para: 80) 
 The Committee also notes the ongoing fleet acquisi tion plans of SCI. The Committee 
recommends that since the financial performances of  the SCI has now improved to a 
certain extent, it may think about more vessel acqu isitions in the near future if the 
International market conditions remain viable. 
(Para: 81) 
NATIONAL WATERWAYS 
 The Committee notes that the IWAI is proposed to un dertake fairway development 
and maintenance of 8 National Ways with an allocati on of Rs. 303 crore during 2017-18. 
The Committee also notes that permission has been g ranted by the Ministry of Shipping to 
raise Rs. 1000 crore through bonds as Extra Budgeta ry Resources and loan from World 
Bank. The Committee may be appraised about the deta ils of funds to be raised through 
bonds, IEBR and loan from World Bank. 
(Para: 87) 
 Cargo movement through Inland Waterways is the mos t economical and 
environment friendly mode of transport. The Committ ee notes that  the growth of cargo 
movement through the IWT mode has not picked up the  required momentum. The 
Committee recommends that all the basic infrastruct ure requirements such as navigation 
channel with sufficient depth and width, day and ni ght navigational aids, terminals for 
berthing of vessel and equipments for loading and u nloading of cargo, etc should be 
provided in all the operational waterways for smoot h cargo handling. The Committee also 
recommends that incentives should be given to those goods carried by waterway mode. 
30

 
 
(Para: 91) 
 The Committee recommends that cargo movement throu gh the water mode need to 
be entertained in all the viable stretches so that the development of national waterways 
may get a  tremendous boost. 
(Para: 92) 
 The Committee notes that the pace of progress of w orks in the various national 
Waterways development are  not up to the mark. The Committee recommends that the 
IWAI should pursue getting various environment clea rances from the concerned 
authorities so that the proposed works may go on smoothly.  
(Para: 93) 
 The Committee notes that the initial studies and p reparation of DPRs of 92 most 
viable National Waterways have been initiated durin g the Financial Year  2017-18. The 
Committee  recommends that necessary funds as required in every stage may be sanctioned 
to IWAI for carrying out the projects work in a vigorous way. 
(Para: 94) 
Promotion of Cruise Shipping 
 The Committee notes that some Major Ports have sta rted giving   incentives to 
cruise ships visiting their Ports. The Committee re commends that apart from incentives, 
the ports may develop good passenger amenities at t he ports and also good passenger 
relations. 
(Para: 97) 
 The Committee also recommends that river cruise to urism may be popularized so 
that waterways tourism may generate more income. Th e Ministry of Shipping should 
coordinate with Ministry of Tourism in their domest ic campaign so that the river cruise 
tourism may get a boost in the coming years. 
(Para: 98) 
General Recommendations 
 The Committee would like to point out that as per the latest economic survey, 
India’s internal trade has a much higher dimension than its international trade. The 
Committee therefore desires that there should be a holistic coordinated approach needed 
for handling of trade within the country as well as  towards openings to the external trade. 
The Committee therefore recommends that the Governm ent should adopt a strategy for 
seamless flow of traffic especially through the National and coastal waterways. 
(Para: 99) 
 The Committee also recommends that the Government would formulate a 
coordinated policy for container size, dimensions a nd such aspects related to container 
traffic. 
(Para: 100) 
  The Committee expressed its apprehension on the i ssue that the entire container 
trade is being controlled by overseas MNCs resultin g in high operational costs to India’s 
internal trade. The Committee observes that transpo rtation in a subcontinent like India 
has to be essentially based on the multimodal syste m. The Committee recommends that a 
high powered inter-ministerial group may be constit uted to take policy decisions on 
internal trade and a high powered regulator for man aging the entire area of logistics of 
container. 
(Para: 101) 
 
31

 
 
 The Committee also recommends that on the lines of  the container corporation of 
India, a coordinated and integrated system for hand ling goods for Railways, Highways, 
Coastal Shipping Inland waterways etc. may be worked out. 
(Para: 102) 
 The Committee notes that a lot of pollutants are d umped into the seas and 
waterways by the vessels in the form of sewages, oi l leakages etc. The Committee 
recommends that Ministry of shipping may take up th e matter under the Swachh Bharat 
Abhiyan seriously and necessary control measures ma y be put in place to prevent 
pollution. 
(Para: 103)

REPORT  
 
Tourism is a major engine of economic growth and an  important source of foreign 
exchange earnings.  It has great capacity to create  large scale employment of diverse kind from 
the most specialized to the unskilled and hence can  play a major role in creation of additional 
employment opportunities.  It can also play an impo rtant role in achieving growth with equity. 
Ministry of Tourism is the nodal agency to formulat e national policies and programmes for the 
development and promotion of tourism in the country . In the process, the Ministry consults and 
collaborates with other stakeholders in the tourism  sector including various Central Ministries 
and other agencies, the State Governments/ Union Te rritory Administrations and representatives 
of the private sector. 
2. The administrative head of the Ministry is the S ecretary (Tourism).  The Secretary also 
acts as the Director General (DG) Tourism. The offi ce of the Director General of Tourism 
provides executive directions for the implementatio n of various policies and programmes.  
Directorate General of Tourism has 20 Domestic fiel d offices and an Indian Institute of Skiing 
and Mountaineering within the country and 14 overse as offices.   The overseas offices promote 
Indian tourism in the market abroad. The domestic f ield offices also play a vital role for 
promotion of tourism sector in the country. They ar e also involved in monitoring the progress of 
implementation of projects sanctioned by the Minist ry to the State Governments/Union 
Territories. 
3. The Ministry of Tourism has under its control a public sector undertaking, the India 
Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) and the following autonomous institutions: 
i. Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Managemen t (IITTM) and National Institute of 
Water Sports (NIWS) 
ii. National Council for Hotel Management and Cater ing Technology (NCHMCT) and the 
Institutes of Hotel Management. 
4. At present there are 42 Institutes of Hotels Man agement (including Central and State 
IHMs), comprising 21 Central IHMS  and 21 State IHM s, and 10 Food Craft Institutes, which  
have come up with the  support of the Ministry. 
5. Tourism is one of the major service industries i n the country. Its contribution in economic 
development and employment generation, particularly  in remote and backward areas, is well 
recognized. As per 2 
nd  Tourism Satellite Account of India (TSA)-2009-10  and subsequent 
estimation for the next three years namely 2010-11,  2011-12 and 2012-13, the contribution of 
tourism to total Gross Domestic Product (GDP) durin g 2009-10,2010-11, 2011-12 and 2012-13 
were 6.77% (3.68% direct and 3.09 indirect), 6.76% (3.67 direct and 3.09% indirect), 6.76% 
(3.67% direct and 3.09% indirect) and 6.88% (3.74% direct and 3.14% indirect), respectively. 
The contribution of tourism to total Employment of the Country during 2009-10,2010-11, 2011-
12 and 2012-13 were 10.17% (4.37% direct and 5.80% indirect), 10.78% (4.63% direct and 
6.15% indirect), 11.49% (4.94% direct and 6.55% indirect) and 12.36% (5.31% direct and 7.05% 
indirect), respectively. 

11 
 
6. India moved 13 positions ahead from 65 th  to 52nd rank in Tourism and Travel 
Competitive Index as per the World Economic Forum (Davos) Report. 
7. The major programmes/ Schemes of the Ministry of  Tourism are:- 
1. Integrated Development of Theme – Based Tourist Circuits – SWADESH DARSHAN 
2. National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spi ritual Augmentation Drive 
(PRASAD) 
3. Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure Development 
4. Assistance for Large Revenue Generating Projects 
5. Overseas Promotion and Publicity including Market Development Assistance 
6. Domestic Promotion and Publicity including Hospitality 
7. Assistance to IHMs/FCIs/IITTM/NIWS 
8. Capacity Building for Service Providers 
9. Computerization and Information Technology 
8. Demand No. 95 containing the details of budgetar y provisions of the Ministry of Tourism

Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure even 50 % of the allocation out of the Rs. 70

Rs. 223.00 crore, the amount spent so far is Rs. 91 .26 crore only.  In case of North East

implementing the schemes and spending of allocation so that the sanctions could be utilized

E-TOURIST VISA 
 
86. The e-Tourist Visa  enables the prospective vis itor to apply for an Indian Visa from 
his/her home country online without visiting the In dian Mission and also pay the visa fee online. 
Once approved, the applicant receives an email auth orizing him/her to travel to India and he/she 
can travel with a print out of this authorization. On arrival, the visitor has to present the 
authorization to the immigration authorities who would then stamp the entry into the country. 
87. Recently, Government of India has approved the proposal regarding further liberalization, 
simplification and rationalization of Visa Regime i n India with a view to facilitate legitimate 
foreign travellers leading to stimulation of econom ic growth increase in earnings from export of 
services and for making various flagship initiatives of the Government successful.  
88. The following changes have been made to E-visa scheme now: 
/square4 The nomenclature of the existing ‘e-Tourist Visa’ h as been changed to ‘e-Visa’ with 
three sub-categories i.e.  ‘e-Tourist Visa’, ‘e-Business Visa’ and ‘e-Medical Visa’. 
The following activities will be permitted under e- Tourist Visa, e-Business Visa  and e-
Medical Visa:- 
 

30 
 
/square4 e-Tourist Visa:  Recreation, sightseeing, casual vi sit to meet friends or relatives, and 
attending a short term yoga programme. 
/square4 e-Business Visa: All activities permitted under nor mal Business Visa as per the Visa 
Manual 
/square4 e-Medical Visa  :Medical treatment, including treat ment under Indian systems of 
medicine. 
/square4 A foreign national will also be permitted to club t hese activities provided he/she had 
clearly indicated the same in the application form along with requisite documents. 
/square4 The window for application under e-Visa stands incr eased from the existing 30 days to 
120 days. 
/square4 Duration of stay in India under e-Visa has been inc reased from the existing 30 days to 60 
days. In the case of e-Medical Visa, extension may be granted up to 6 months on case to 
case basis on merits of each case by the Foreigners  Regional Registration Officer 
(FRRO)/ Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO) concerned. 
/square4 On e-Tourist Visa and e-Business Visa, a foreign na tional will be permitted double entry 
as against single entry at present. In the case of those availing e-Medical Visa, triple entry 
will be permitted as against single entry at present. 
Grant of e-Visa will be subject to the following conditions:- 
/square4 e-Visa will be non-extendable except in the case of  e-Medical Visa as mentioned in sub-
para (3) above. 
/square4 e-Visa will be non-convertible to any other types of visa except in the following cases:- 
89. To ‘X’ (Entry) Visa if a foreigner who has come  to India on an e-visa marries an Indian 
national during the validity of his/her e-Visa. Thi s will be subject to submission of a copy of the 
registered Marriage Certificate and a report about their marital status which will, inter-alia, 
include his/her antecedents, confirmation about their living together and security clearance. 
90. To Medical (MED) Visa if a foreigner falls ill after his/her entry into India rendering 
him/her unfit to travel and who requires specialized medical treatment provided he/she is eligible 
for the grant of Medical Visa and a medical certifi cate is obtained from a government / ICMR 
(Indian Council of Medical Research) / NABH (Nation al Accreditation Board for Hospitals  & 
Healthcare Providers  / MCI (Medical Council of Ind ia)/ CGHS (Central Government Health 
Scheme) recognized hospital. 
91. To ‘X’ (Entry) Visa in the case of a Person of Indian Origin who is otherwise entitled for 
‘X’ (Entry) Visa. Restriction of one application pe r email ID per month has been  removed.  E-
Visa will be provided at 5 major Indian Ports i.e. Mumbai, Cochin,  Goa, Chennai and 
Mangalore to tap the potential of cruise tourists  from different countries.

The Committee recommends that Uttarakhand, Himachal  Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil 
Nadu also may be projected through the incredible India 2.0 campaign. 
(Para:69) 
 The Committee observes that the Ministry of Touris m has an Overseas Promotion 
and Publicity Policy.  Under that, a number of Memo randa of Understanding are signed 
with a number of Countries. Indo-Taiwanese Parliame ntary Forum had a meeting 
recently. Taiwanese Parliamentary Delegation and Trade Delegation had come here during 
that time and in August, Indian delegation had gone  there.  It was noted that there is a 
need of a tourism office in Taiwan which would enab le more tourists from Taiwan to visit 
India. So far,  India is not properly marketed in T aiwan. The Committee notes that though 
India does not have full diplomatic relations with Taiwan but we should not hesitate to 
conduct publicity road shows to attract Taiwanese t ourists. The Committee therefore, 

42 
 
recommends that India Tourism office abroad may tak e necessary initiatives in Taiwan in 
this regard.  
(Para:70) 
TRAINING AND SKILL DEVELOPMENT   
 The Committee notes the various training activitie s the Ministry of Tourism carried 
out during 2016-17. The Committee recommends that t he Ministry of Tourism should 
ensure that the trained students get better placements in the tourism industry. 
(Para:79) 
 The Committee also notes that guidelines for Hunar  Se Rozgar Tak programme are 
still  under revision in consultation with Ministry  of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship to bring the programme in conformi ty with the common norms of the 
skill development of National Vocational Qualificat ion framework and thereby, the HSRT 
programme has been suspended. The delay in formulat ion of guidelines is unacceptable. 
The Committee desires that the guidelines may be re framed at the earliest so that, the 
HSRT programme may train job aspirants. 
(Para:80) 
 The Committee notes that Budget allocation for CBS P Scheme for the year 2017-18 
is Rs. 65.00 crore with a  target to train 86000 tr ainees in the Hunar Se Rozgar Tak and 
Skill Testing and Certification courses. The Commit tee strongly desires that the Ministry 
of Tourism would be able to accomplish the target to train 86000 youths under various skill 
testing and certification courses. 
(Para:81) 
 The Committee during its various study visits came  to know that the adequacy of 
trained tourist guides all over the country are far  from required numbers.  The Committee 
notes that the tourism industry is growing day by d ay and the tourist flow has also 
increased in many folds.  In order to meet the exis ting requirement of qualified tourist 
guides, the Committee feels that the present course s and training facilities are inadequate.  
The Committee, therefore, recommends that more   in stitutions to train the tourist guides 
should be opened in the country to facilitate the tourists. 
(Para:82) 
 The Committee also notes that some people are posi ng as Government approved 
tourists guides in the important tourist places car rying fake identity cards and thereby 
misguiding tourists.  Their only aim is to fleece t he tourists in one form or the other.  The 
Committee also notes that such people are defaming the Brand name of India among the 
national/international tourists visiting tourist pl aces.  The Committee recommends that 
stringent action should be taken against such peopl e who are posing as tourist guides.  The 
Committee recommends that a standardized identity card with a particular logo and colour 
code may be formulated for the certified guides thr oughout the country.  And such an 
identity card may be advertised in the publicity ca mpaigns to improve the trust quotient of 
the tourist guides. 
(Para:83) 
 The Committee also recommends that efforts may be made to increase the 
availability of foreign language experts in the cou ntry.  Prominent institutes in the country 
may be encouraged to impart such training, by giving incentives for running the courses. 
(Para:84) 
        The Committee observes that many students a re not able to take up the courses under 
the Culinary Institute and other Hotel Management I nstitutions because of the insistence 
that it is a composite course and that one has to pass even the non-vegetarian cuisine. Many 

43 
 
people have been representing this matter to Member s of Parliament saying that the 
Government should reconsider this issue and not to be insisted on non-vegetarian cuisine.  
The Committee recommends that there should have a s eparate branch for vegetarian and 
non-vegetarian cuisine in the Culinary Institutes and Hotel Management Institutions where 
ever such institutes are there in the country.  
(Para:85) 
E-TOURIST VISA  
 The Committee notes the recent changes made by the  Government in the e-visa 
norms. The Committee also notes that introduction o f e-visa facilities to more countries 
have increased the foreign tourist arrivals in the country.  The Committee recommends 
that the Ministry of Tourism, for introduction of  e-visa facilities in more airports and 
seaports, the budgetary support may be provided on need basis.  
(Para:94) 
CRUISE TOURISM  
 The Committee observes that cruise tourism is one of the most dynamic and the 
fastest growing components of the leisure industry worldwide. It is fast emerging as a new 
marketable product. India with its vast and beautif ul coastline, virgin forests and 
undisturbed idyllic islands, rich historical and cu ltural heritage, can be a fabulous tourist 
destination for cruise tourists. With the Indian ec onomy developing at a steady pace, 
middle class growing in number and increasingly pos sessing disposable incomes which 
could be spent on leisure activities, the domestic tourists also could take on cruise shipping 
in a big way. 
(Para:98) 
 The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism h as not done much for 
promotion of cruise tourism in the country as only three projects are so far funded by them 
in the last two years.  The country has vast potent ial for cruise tourism.  All the major 
ports can attract cruise vessels from most parts of the country as well as world operators.   
(Para:99) 
 The Committee notes the initiatives taken by the m eeting chaired by the  Prime 
Minister wherein the Ministries of Shipping and Tou rism have been entrusted with 
identifying viable routes for cruise tourism promot ion.  The Committee recommends that 
the 9 tourist circuits identified by the Working Gr oup along the NW-1 & NW-2 may be 
developed as early as possible.  The Committee reco mmends that sufficient allocations may 
be made for the purpose  from the appropriate heads. 
(Para:100) 
 The Committee notes that other than NW-1 & NW-2, t here are many routes which 
could be utilized for developing cruise circuits in  the country.  The Ministry has not yet 
explored the possibility of NW-3 for this purpose.  The Committee knows that the Cochin 
Port is receiving good number of cruise vessels and the port has made specific efforts in this 
regard to enhance the tourist footfalls there.  The  Committee recommends that all the 
required facilities may be developed at Cochin Port to enable the exclusive cruise berth and 
other facilities to attract more cruise vessels. 
(Para:101) 
 The possibility of cruise tourism may be explored in Andamans and Nicobar  and 
Lakshadweep without disturbing the environment and eco system.  
(Para:102) 
 
 

44 
 
CONNECTIVITY  
 The Committee notes that many a times the Ministry  of Tourism has informed the 
Parliament that reviving airstrips is the duty of M inistry of Civil Aviation.  The Committee 
notes that Ministry of Tourism being aware of tourism potential and possibilities of various 
parts of the country is in a better position to adv ise and cooperate with the Ministry of 
Civil Aviation to identify the airstrips for reviva l.  The Civil Aviation Policy has 
enumerated revival of airstrips as one of its items .  The Ministry of Tourism should utilize 
this opportunity and in coordination with Ministry of Civil Aviation should identify all 
possible airstrips for revival to expand tourism in the country. 
(Para:104) 
 The Committee observes that with the special natur e of topographical and 
geographical conditions of the major tourist attrac tions in the country, which are spread 
among various States, travel from one State to anot her is must for the tourists visiting the 
country.  Most of the tourists desire to visit mult iple destinations at the same trip for which 
they require smooth travel from one place to anothe r.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that Ministry of Road Transport and High ways may introduce the online 
system for granting All India permit to tourist veh icles, allowing seamless travel of the 
tourist vehicles across the country at the earliest.  
(Para:106) 
 The Committee notes the initiatives taken to upgra de 24 railway stations in the 
country.  The Committee desires that all the railwa y station connecting the tourist 
destinations should have neat and clean tourist ame nities, well staffed help desks and 
information counters.  The Committee also recommend s that railway staff/porters may be 
trained to facilities the tourists. 
(Para:110) 
 The Committee also notes that introduction of peni nsular tourism trains in the 
southern zone has been taken for discussion by the Standing Committee constituted for the 
purpose.  The Committee recommends that the Ministr y of Tourism may take further 
initiatives so that all the southern States may pro mptly submit their proposals for 
consideration of the Committee. 
(Para:111) 
 The Committee notes that cleanliness has an import ant role to play in promoting 
tourism.  The Swatch Bharat Mission has a great rol e to play in this regard. A large 
number of tourists both domestic and foreign are us ing the Railway Stations for their 
travel.  Unfortunately our railway Stations have du e to open toilets remain dirty and 
smelly.  The stink of the railway stations are awful and strong that  the people can stay/wait  
at the railway platforms only by closing their nost rils.  This is happening mainly due to the 
use of toilets by the passengers while the train is  halted at the railway stations.  The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism s hould take necessary step in 
coordination with Ministry of Railways to introduce  controlled discharge toilet systems 
(CDTS) and bio toilets or zero discharge toilet sys tems (ZDTS)  in all the trains of Indian 
Railways.  Adequate media publicity may be given to   discourage people from using the 
toilets of the train while the train is halted at t he Railway Station. The Ministry of Tourism 
may take up this issue with the Ministry of Railways for necessary action. 
(Para:112) 
 The Committee notes that Helicopter connectivity is  an important aspect to connect 
various tourist places and to meet the requirement of high end tourists and also places 
which are difficult to access otherwise.  Even thos e places which are connected by road and 

45 
 
rail, the tourists will enjoy helicopter rides if i t is affordable and easily available.  The 
Committee further notes that the Ministry of touris m has written letters to the Ministry of 
Civil Aviation to start helicopter operations and t he latter has not responded so far.  The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism s hould interact with the Cabinet 
Secretary and the Prime Minister’s Office to ensure  that Ministry of civil Aviation is 
responding favourably to start helicopter operation s at various tourist places with the 
assistance of Pawan Hans Limited.  
(Para:114) 
 The Committee desires that the entire major touris t destinations should have 
helicopter connectivity with affordable fare struct ure so that common people may also 
travel to visit important tourist destinations. 
(Para:115) 
 The Committee notes that Andaman and Nicobar Islan ds are attracting both 
domestic and international tourists. However, the i nter connectivity in these islands are 
very poor as compared to the actual need.  The Comm ittee recommends that Ministry of 
Tourism may take up this issue with the concerned M inistries to improve the inter 
connectivity of various islands of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.  
(Para:116) 
 The Committee also reminds the requirement of deve loping easy access and  
connectivity to Gir Forest in Gujarat.  The air con nectivity is also not very good.  The 
Committee is aware of the fact  that there is an op erational airport near the Gir Forest 
which if developed properly could be utilized for o perating tourist chartered flights and 
regular domestic flights.  The Committee recommends  that Ministry of Tourism may 
explore the possibility through the Ministry of Civil Aviation to operationalise airports.  
(Para:117) 
 The Committee also recommends that last mile conne ctivity to all tourist 
destinations especially in the North-Eastern States  may be developed in coordination with 
the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. 
(Para:118) 
Safety and Security of Tourists  
 The Committee notes the steps taken by the Ministr y of Tourism in addressing the  
safety and security concerns of the tourists visiti ng the country. The Committee notes that 
after 2014 there was  no meeting of the States and UTs held to review the status of security 
of tourists in the country.  The Committee also not es the steps taken by the Ministry of 
Tourism to safe guard the tourists.  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should 
convene meetings of  Tourism Ministers of States an d UTs at regular intervals to review of 
the status of security of tourists. 
(Para:121) 
 The Committee also notes that with the popularizat ion of smart phones and the 
social media, the young people in particular and th e general public in general are engaged 
in taking selfies wherever they go.  As per the rec ent news reports, many mishaps were 
occured at tourists places while people  were engag ed in taking risky photographs.  The 
Committee notes the steps taken by the Ministry of Tourism in discouraging such people.  
The Committee recommends that strict penalty   may be imposed  if anybody found taking 
selfie in danger zone area and violating  the rule.  
(Para:122) 
 
 

46 
 
India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC)  
 The Committee is happy to note that ITDC has been making profits continuously 
during the last five years. 
(Para:127) 
 The Committee also appreciates ITDC’s effort to in troduce Light and Sound Show 
at various monuments and tourist places across the country. The Committee recommends 
that Ministry of Tourism should extend required fin ancial support to extend from its 
available funds for the venture as the light and so und shows attracts a large number of 
tourists and it act as  a catalyst  agent for tourism promotion.  
(Para:128) 
 The Committee   notes that Ross Island in Andaman has excellent light and sound 
system. However, at the Cellular Jail the light and  sound show needs improvement. The 
Committee recommends that the light and sound  show  of Cellular Jail may be revamped 
in a proper manner to show case our history. 
(Para:129) 
 The Committee notes that standard of hotel accommo dation in Andaman is poor 
compared to other places.  The Committee recommends  that necessary steps may be taken 
by the Ministry of Tourism to fill the gap. 
(Para:130) 
 The Committee also notes that there are so many to urist places in the country where 
we don’t have proper infrastructure, toilet facilit ies, waste disposal facilities, proper 
signage and guidelines to tourists. The Committee d esires that apart from constructing 
certain buildings on a temporary basis, it is the d uty of the Ministry of Tourism to ensure 
that the said facilities may be made  available thr oughout the year to the tourists. For 
maintenance of the said facility, the Ministry of T ourism may keep a separate fund. The 
efforts of the Ministry should be to make the visit s of tourists a pleasant one and the 
tourists may visit again to these places. 
(Para:131) 
 The Committee feels that an effective co-ordinatio n mechanism among the Ministry 
of Tourism, Ministries of Culture, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways, Railways, 
Shipping and Home Affairs is needed in order to ens ure that the places of tourist and 
cultural importance are integrated with well connec ted roads, railways and airports and 
are provided with required facilities like budget h otels, taxis, souvenir shops, restaurants, 
tourist guides and security to tourists. The Commit tee therefore recommends that the 
Ministry of Tourism may co-ordinate in formulating an action plan with the above said 
Ministries in this regard and that the Ministry of Tourism may be made the nodal Ministry 
for this purpose. 
(Para:132)
